title: Institutions pile back into US Bitcoin ETFs in Q3 after selling streak
summary: Asset managers added the equivalent of 49,229 Bitcoin to their US Bitcoin ETF holdings in the third quarter, reversing three quarters of net selling.
content:
Institutional investment managers’ holdings of US Bitcoin exchange-traded funds climbed to a record high in the third quarter, as they reversed three straight quarters of net selling, according to regulatory filings.

The 13F filings, analyzed by Galaxy Research, show that the reporting companies added an equivalent of 49,229 Bitcoin (BTC) in the third quarter, outpacing the 47,054 Bitcoin they shed over the last three quarters combined. This lifted the reported total holdings to 356,491 BTC, the highest on record.

“The quarter’s accumulation was the work of a few dozen large institutions,” wrote Galaxy’s head of firmwide research Alex Thorn.

Quarterly 13F filings provide a point-in-time snapshot of US-listed securities held by reporting institutional investment managers. Thorn said half of the net addition of spot Bitcoin ETF shares came from advisors and wealth platforms.

Wells Fargo posted the largest increase, adding the equivalent of 14,636 Bitcoin, making it the largest institutional holder of spot Bitcoin ETPs. Other strong gainers included Brevan Howard, Bank of America, Millennium Management and Jane Street.

“Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot Bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi previously told Cointelegraph, when the first batch of 13F filings had begun to come in.

The number of managers reporting a position in a spot Bitcoin ETF also rose for the first time in three quarters, increasing by 191 to 2,166.

This all came as Bitcoin gained about 43% in the third quarter, ending September at $83,621.

Related: Bitcoin ETF assets fall to three-month low as 2026 net outflows top $2.5B

Meanwhile, Galaxy’s data shows BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for the largest share of holdings reported by 13F filers, with the equivalent of 232,453 BTC held by the filers. This was followed by the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund.

Together, the two funds were responsible for 77% of all Bitcoin held by the reporting entities.

US Bitcoin ETFs post two months of outflows

The record institutional holdings in Q3 contrast with more recent weakness in US spot Bitcoin ETFs, with net monthly outflows reaching $515 million in October and $2.9 billion of outflows month to date, according to TFTC’s Bitcoin ETF tracker.

Earlier in the month, Bitwise head of research André Dragosch told Cointelegraph he viewed the selling as “related to a short-term risk-off environment rather than a structural change in institutional sentiment.”

title: CME’s XRP Futures Hit $81.2 Billion After 18 Months of Trading
summary: CME Group’s XRP and Micro XRP futures reached $81.2 billion in trading volume over roughly 18 months. Trading across the two products totaled 1.9 million contracts. XRP Futures Averaged $216 Million a Day CME Group (Nasdaq: CME) reported $81.2 billion in notional XRP futures volume Nov. 19 for its s...
content:
CME Group’s XRP and Micro XRP futures reached $81.2 billion in trading volume over roughly 18 months. Trading across the two products totaled 1.9 million contracts.

Key Takeaways

  • XRP and Micro XRP futures averaged $216 million in daily notional volume on CME.
  • Trading volume represented the equivalent of 42.8 billion XRP.
  • CME introduced options on both contract sizes in October 2025.

XRP Futures Averaged $216 Million a Day

CME Group (Nasdaq: CME) reported $81.2 billion in notional XRP futures volume Nov. 19 for its standard and micro contracts through Nov. 16. The exchange shared the recap on X, citing average daily notional volume of $216 million.

The notional total reflects the full underlying value of the contracts, which can change hands multiple times. For these crypto derivatives tied to an underlying asset, the dollar total and the 42.8 billion XRP equivalent express the same trading activity in different units.

CME highlighted its lead in open interest, which measures the contracts outstanding at a given time. Coinglass data on XRP futures put CME first among the exchanges it tracked, with about 18.5% of open interest at 12:03 p.m. EST on Nov. 19.

From the First Block Trade to 1.9 Million Contracts

The first trade in CME XRP futures took place on May 18, 2025, and prime broker Hidden Road cleared the privately negotiated block transaction. Ripple had announced a deal to acquire Hidden Road in April 2025 and completed the acquisition in October 2025, when Hidden Road became Ripple Prime. CME recorded more than $19 million in notional volume on the first day.

Each standard contract represents 50,000 XRP, the equivalent of 20 micro contracts of 2,500 XRP each. Both settle in cash against the CME CF XRP-Dollar Reference Rate, a daily benchmark for XRP’s price in U.S. dollars. CME cited 9,900 XRP and Micro XRP futures contracts for Oct. 27, 2025, a daily record at the time.

CME’s third-quarter crypto report put notional volume for its broader XRP futures and options suite at $10.1 billion for the three months through September 2026. The exchange listed an average of 12,200 contracts a day for that suite.

CME Added Options and Spot-Quoted Futures

Crypto market maker Wintermute and securities tokenization firm Superstate executed the first trade in options on CME’s XRP futures on Oct. 12, 2025, about five months after the underlying futures debuted. CME announced the first transaction two days later and listed daily, monthly, and quarterly expirations.

The XRP options rollout covered both contract sizes, giving traders a choice in how much XRP exposure each option represents. Buyers pay a premium for the right to take a position in the corresponding futures contract at a specified price.

The exchange introduced spot-quoted XRP futures on Dec. 15, 2025, with a longer-dated expiry that removes the need to periodically roll positions. Traders negotiate its price near the underlying XRP spot index.

A daily financing adjustment in the spot-quoted futures design accounts for the gap between the underlying spot index and the corresponding lead-month futures price. CME adds the accumulated adjustment to the agreed spot price to determine the cleared futures position price.

title: ‘Scattered Spider’ Hacker Gets 6 Years in Prison for $11.6M Crypto Theft Scheme
summary: Phishing texts sent to company employees helped a group of hackers steal at least $11.6 million in cryptocurrency from people across the United States. Tyler Robert Buchanan received six years in federal prison, completing sentencing for all five defendants in the case. Buchanan Receives Six-Year Se...
content:
Phishing texts sent to company employees helped a group of hackers steal at least $11.6 million in cryptocurrency from people across the United States. Tyler Robert Buchanan received six years in federal prison, completing sentencing for all five defendants in the case.

Key Takeaways

  • At least $11.6 million in cryptocurrency was stolen from U.S. victims.
  • Phishing at 12 or more companies supplied data used to target individuals.
  • A Dec. 11 hearing will address restitution after the final sentencing.

Buchanan Receives Six-Year Sentence

Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month federal prison sentence on Nov. 17 for his role in a conspiracy that stole at least $11.6 million in cryptocurrency. U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb scheduled a restitution hearing for Dec. 11.

Buchanan pleaded guilty on April 17 to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. He has been in federal custody since April 2025 and was the fifth and final defendant sentenced in the case. The criminal activity described in his plea agreement ran from September 2021 to April 2023. Buchanan was publicly linked to the cybercrime group Scattered Spider by October 2024, when an HHS threat profile of the group listed him among its associated arrested members.

The conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least 12 companies. The messages appeared to come from their employers or contracted service providers and directed recipients to lookalike websites, where the attackers collected usernames, passwords, and other personal information.

Prosecutors stated in a sentencing memorandum:

“Those thefts had severe, life-altering consequences for many victims and underscore both the seriousness and far-reaching impact of this conspiracy.”

How Company Intrusions Led to Crypto Theft

Stolen employee credentials opened access to company accounts and systems. The group took confidential information, including names, email addresses, telephone numbers, and account credentials, then used data from those intrusions to identify and access individual victims’ cryptocurrency accounts and wallets.

A phishing kit forwarded captured employee login credentials to a Telegram channel administered by Buchanan and another conspirator. Investigators also found company files and victims’ personal information on a device at Buchanan’s residence in Scotland, including a text file with crypto seed phrases and login details for one victim’s account.

To bypass text-message authentication, the conspirators transferred victims’ phone numbers to devices they controlled, allowing them to intercept verification codes. The FCC’s description of SIM-swap fraud, released in November 2023, explains how a fraudulent transfer redirects calls and texts. The commission’s order addressed carrier safeguards against such transfers.

Fraudulent login pages can impersonate a company and collect credentials from people who believe they are using a legitimate website. Visiting the company’s website directly instead of following a link in an unsolicited message reduces that exposure.

Separate Cases Show the Wider Risk

In an October 2026 incident, a breach at a Coinbase analytics provider exposed some customer contact information. Coinbase said it found no evidence of unauthorized access to its systems and that customer funds were not impacted. The case illustrates how information held outside an exchange can create opportunities for impersonation and targeted phishing.

Another case involved a Justice Department effort to forfeit more than $5 million in bitcoin in September 2025. Prosecutors alleged that attackers used SIM swaps to access five victims’ cryptocurrency accounts and moved the stolen assets through a casino platform. That proceeding is unrelated to Buchanan’s conspiracy.

A SIM-swap theft led to a $33 million arbitration award against T-Mobile reported in March 2025. The victim’s lawyers said the carrier paid the award, which included fees, interest, and costs. In Buchanan’s case, the court will take up restitution at its Dec. 11 hearing.

title: Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet to leave after nine years at company
summary: Guillemet helped establish Ledger’s Donjon security lab and says his departure has been planned for months.
content:
Ledger chief technology officer Charles Guillemet announced he will be leaving the company at the end of 2026, after nine years at the company.

In a post on LinkedIn on Thursday, Guillemet said he joined as chief security officer in December 2017, around three years after Ledger was founded. He launched Ledger Donjon, the company’s attack lab, a year later.

“We’ve been preparing this transition for many months, so Ledger’s teams, partners and roadmaps are ready. I’m bullish on Ledger’s future,” said Guillemet.

Guillemet has been a central figure in Ledger’s security operations, first as chief security officer and later as chief technology officer. He helped establish the Ledger Donjon attack lab, which tests hardware and software vulnerabilities. According to Guillemet, Ledger devices now secure roughly 20% of the world’s crypto assets.

“The threat landscape changed too. AI is making attacks cheaper, faster and easier to scale,” he added.

“The question we spent a decade answering for crypto (how do you protect what matters when any device can be compromised?) is now a question for every company, every AI agent and every government.”

Guillemet did not disclose details of his next venture but said he was “building something new” and would “dedicate my time to solving this security mess.”

Guillemet’s announcement comes weeks after Ledger disclosed that attackers had modified genuine hardware wallets with hidden components designed to capture users’ recovery phrases, and slipped the devices into authorized resellers.

The tampering cases were initially reported in Asia, with subsequent incidents identified in Europe and the United Arab Emirates.

title: Moonpay Seeks US Bank Charter as Crypto Firms Expand Into Federally Regulated Finance
summary: Crypto payments company Moonpay has applied for a national trust bank charter, joining a growing list of digital asset firms seeking federal banking oversight as they expand into stablecoin services and institutional custody.   Moonpay has applied to establish a federally regulated trust bank in the...
content:
Crypto payments company Moonpay has applied for a national trust bank charter, joining a growing list of digital asset firms seeking federal banking oversight as they expand into stablecoin services and institutional custody.

Key Takeaways

  • Moonpay has applied for a U.S. national trust bank charter, seeking OCC approval to offer digital asset custody, stablecoin issuance, redemption, and reserve management.
  • Moonpay joins a growing list of crypto firms pursuing federal banking oversight, including Coinbase, Circle, Ripple, and Stripe-owned Bridge.
  • The application follows Moonpay’s aggressive expansion into stablecoins and tokenization.

Moonpay has applied to establish a federally regulated trust bank in the United States, becoming the latest cryptocurrency company to pursue a banking charter under the Trump administration’s increasingly favorable regulatory environment for digital assets.

The company submitted its application to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) on Nov. 17, according to regulatory documents, and the agency recorded its receipt the following day. The proposed Moonpay National Trust Bank would be headquartered in Miami Beach, Florida, and operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Moonpay Inc.

If approved, the institution would offer digital asset custody and stablecoin services, including issuance, redemption, and management of reserves backing digital currencies. It would also provide conversion services on behalf of clients.

Unlike conventional commercial banks, the proposed institution would not accept deposits or extend traditional loans. Instead, the non-depository trust bank would operate under federal supervision, providing specialized financial services without Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. (FDIC) coverage.

Moonpay co-founder and CEO Ivan Soto-Wright would chair the proposed bank’s five-member board and serve as interim president and chief executive. Other organizers include co-founder Victor Faramond, MoonPay CFO Anne Giviskos, Michael Lempres, and Caroline Butler.

The application also outlines a digital-first operating model, with no public-facing offices or plans to establish branches during its first three years. Moonpay says it serves more than 30 million customers across 180 countries and supports more than 500 enterprise clients.

Crypto Firms Race for Federal Bank Charters

Moonpay’s application follows a wave of similar moves by cryptocurrency companies seeking to bring custody, stablecoin operations, and other financial services under federal banking supervision.

As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, Coinbase received final OCC approval for its national trust bank on Nov. 6, following conditional authorization in April. The approval allows Coinbase to operate its institutional custody business under a federal regulatory framework without becoming a conventional deposit-taking bank.

Stablecoin issuer Circle and payments company Ripple also secured federal trust bank approvals earlier this year, while Stripe-owned Bridge received conditional authorization in February. Other applicants have included institutional crypto exchange EDX Markets, digital asset infrastructure provider Zerohash, and Wall Street banking giant Morgan Stanley.

For Moonpay, the federal application builds on regulatory progress at the state level. In November 2025, the company received a limited-purpose trust charter from New York’s Department of Financial Services, expanding its authorization to provide institutional digital asset custody and over-the-counter trading services.

The company had previously secured New York’s BitLicense, strengthening its position among cryptocurrency businesses operating under the state’s regulatory framework.

Moonpay Accelerates Expansion Into Stablecoins and Tokenization

The charter application also follows several major initiatives aimed at expanding Moonpay’s business beyond its original focus on helping customers purchase cryptocurrency.

In September, Moonpay announced plans to acquire North Capital Investment Technology, a transaction designed to add regulated brokerage, investment advisory, and alternative trading system capabilities to its infrastructure. The deal would strengthen Moonpay’s ability to support tokenized securities and other traditional financial products represented on blockchain networks.

Moonpay also partnered with asset manager WisdomTree to expand access to tokenized Treasury products, including plans to incorporate the firm’s blockchain-based money market fund into stablecoin reserve management.

Internationally, Moonpay launched a South Korean subsidiary in September, working with Kakaobank, Woori Bank, and KB Financial Group on stablecoin payments, remittances, and related banking services. It subsequently announced a partnership with Dunamu, the parent company of crypto exchange Upbit, to explore stablecoin-powered cross-border payments and corporate treasury applications.

The proposed federal charter would provide another regulated foundation for those ambitions, potentially allowing Moonpay to offer custody and stablecoin infrastructure directly through a nationally supervised institution.

However, the application remains subject to OCC review, and approval is not guaranteed. The company must satisfy regulatory requirements before its proposed trust bank can begin operations.

For Moonpay and its competitors, the growing pursuit of banking charters reflects a broader shift in the cryptocurrency industry, as companies that once operated largely outside traditional finance seek to become part of its regulated infrastructure.

title: Babylon Weighs End to Bitcoin Staking—What Happens to $2.6B in BTC?
summary: Babylon co-founder Fisher Yu’s suggestion to end bitcoin staking on the protocol adds another unknown to an already exhausted market, putting a question mark over about 41,600 BTC (nearly $2.6 billion) staked there. On Tuesday, Nov. 17, Babylon co-founder Fisher Yu suggested ending its BTC staking p...
content:
Babylon co-founder Fisher Yu’s suggestion to end bitcoin staking on the protocol adds another unknown to an already exhausted market, putting a question mark over about 41,600 BTC (nearly $2.6 billion) staked there.

Key Takeaways

  • Babylon co-founder Fisher Yu proposed ending BTC staking by the end of 2026 to focus on its Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV) protocol.
  • About 41,600 BTC (nearly $2.6 billion) is staked on Babylon, with roughly 80% delegated to two Kraken-run providers.
  • With staking yields down to 0.03%–0.5%, it’s unclear what holders will do with their BTC on Babylon.

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, Babylon co-founder Fisher Yu suggested ending its BTC staking program by the end of this year so the platform can focus more on its Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV) protocol. This is only a suggestion intended to initiate a discussion in the Babylon community, though it could eventually lead to a vote. At the time of writing, no one had replied to Yu’s forum post.

“TBV is a much more powerful and versatile protocol for putting native bitcoin to work than bitcoin staking,” Yu said, adding that TBV “requires a lot more engineering and security work, and the Babylon team’s full attention.” Yu added that ending bitcoin staking would also let Babylon cut BABY token inflation from 5.5% to 2%.

According to Yu, “the sunset should be relatively straightforward,” and once unstaked, users “can choose to put their BTC to work through TBV applications.”

This is where the uncertainty comes in, as no one knows for sure what the holders of about 41,600 BTC will do with these billions of dollars’ worth of bitcoin.

Gradual Unlock and Kraken’s Dominance

If the sunset is confirmed, then it wouldn’t mean that all the staked BTC would be unlocked at once. Currently, a staker can exit early if Babylon’s committee co-signs the request. This takes about two to seven days. Alternatively, stakers can wait until their original lock expires, which can take up to about 15 months from the stake date. That means these funds could become available at different times.

Kraken, which offers bitcoin staking on Babylon to its clients, currently dominates the protocol. About 80% of the staked BTC is delegated to two Kraken-run providers, according to Babylon’s data. If the sunset is approved and Kraken unstakes, then that BTC would likely return to clients’ Kraken accounts. Clients could then move it into TBV—which would likely require first withdrawing it to their own wallets, since TBV vaults are self-custodial—or sell it, hold it, or use it in other ways, such as spending it.

Staking Offers Little Yield at 0.03%–0.5%

However, nothing stops users from doing the same now, especially as staking rewards have dropped to almost zero: Babylon’s dashboard shows a BTC staking APR of 0.03% to 0.5%.

Why users continue to keep BTC on the platform despite such low rewards is unknown. It may suggest that many are passive holders who are unlikely to rush to sell or redeploy their bitcoin once staking ends, though this is only speculation. For example, in August, Lombard—one of Babylon’s largest users—switched its LBTC yield strategy from Babylon staking to a covered-call strategy managed by Bitwise.

Opportunities on Aave

Babylon’s co-founder also noted that Aave governance backed a proposal on Nov. 9 to enable native BTC as collateral through TBV. Once live, it would let bitcoin holders borrow stablecoins from Aave V4’s main liquidity pool. A final Aave vote is still needed before launch. According to Yu, TBV’s mainnet is expected to start in a permissioned, private phase in late November before opening to everyone in early 2027.

Babylon also said the integration with Aave could bring new opportunities for BTC holders. Solutions already being tested include Aegis’ fixed-rate borrowing application, which leverages stablecoin vaults to hedge Aave’s variable rates, and Cradle’s options DEX. The latter allows BTC holders to generate yield by selling covered-call spread options against their bitcoin, Babylon said.

Babylon also noted that the Aave integration would allow users to generate yield by deploying borrowed stablecoins into other yield opportunities and earning the carry—the difference between their cost of borrowing stablecoins and the yield they earn.

Some initial reactions favor the sunset, as bitcoin lending is gaining momentum while BTC staking offers minuscule annual percentage returns.

BABY Price Is Down 95%

According to Defillama data, Babylon ranks second among restaking protocols by total value locked, accounting for 36% of the total. Meanwhile, the BABY token is down 62% over the past 12 months and approximately 95% from its all-time high, reached in April 2025.

All that said, while ending BTC staking on Babylon might change nothing for the market in terms of BTC available for trading, the fact remains that more than $2 billion worth of bitcoin sits on a platform where it earns almost nothing, at a time when the bitcoin market has tanked.

title: Binance’s $6.5B freeze order, Hong Kong ‘suspicious’ of HYPE: Asia Express
summary: Binance obtains court orders freezing assets stolen in October’s hack. Hong Kong warns citizens about Hyperliquid, and Thai police arrest four foreigners linked to a crypto scam.
content:
Binance obtains $6.5B global freeze order, plans to expand throughout Asia

Binance has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing injunction from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts as it seeks to recover assets stolen in its record Oct. 29 hack.

The court orders target unidentified perpetrators of the attack and are intended to help issuers, exchanges and other partners freeze and return stolen assets,

The orders can be served via blockchain, allowing legal notices to be delivered to wallet addresses rather than through traditional channels. Market participants will also be notified of updates to a “living list” of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets.

Despite losing billions in the hack, Binance’s APAC head SB Seker told Reuters this week its finances are sound and it plans to expand throughout South East Asia.

“We have ongoing conversations with at least five or six markets ... three of which are in quite mature stages,” he said. Binance currently has operating licenses in 15 markets.

Source: Binance

HONG KONG

Hong Kong adds Hyperliquid to list of ‘suspicious’ crypto platforms

Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added decentralized perps exchange Hyperliquid to its Alert List. The SFC said Hyperliquid lacks a license to operate in the city and is suspected of actively marketing its services to the region’s public.

The SFC is now officially suspicious of 69 platforms.

More Hong Kong news

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Swift will explore linking the HKMA’s market infrastructure, Project Ensemble, with Swift’s ledger, for cross-border payments using tokenized deposits in multiple currencies.

SINGAPORE

Singapore settles $77.5M tokenized bill sale with wholesale CBDC

The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) issued 100 million Singapore dollars ($77.5 million) in tokenized bills on Nov. 6, with banks using wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC) to pay for them. Five banks submitted bids totaling more than twice the amount on offer, MAS said Thursday. The four-week bills mature on Dec. 4.

MAS issued the bills directly on the Singapore Dollar Test Network. That gives borrowers an asset they could pledge as collateral for loans on the network, the central bank said.

Source: Pexels

More Singapore news

Singapore’s DBS has partnered with Circle to broaden customer access to USDC across Asia.

CryptoJobsList has acquired its rival crypto jobs service Crypto.jobs.

Wisdom Tree has registered three tokenized funds in Singapore and is working with Synthesys to make them available through regulated intermediaries.

Citadel Securities is expanding its Singapore and Sydney offices by 40% and 65% respectively.

CHINA

Shanghai says yes to blockchain but CAC says no to ICO and exchange names

The Shanghai Municipal Science and Technology Commission and the Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Data have issued a new policy that encourages the adoption of blockchain and other technologies as a way to share and track scientific data.

Meanwhile the Cyberspace Administration of China has clarified the names of blockchain information services are not allowed to include words like “virtual currency”, “exchange” and “ICO”

VIETNAM

Bunge and CP Group expand blockchain soy traceability to Vietnam

Agribusiness solutions company Bunge and feed ingredient trading firm Bangkok Produce Merchandising Company have expanded their blockchain based soy traceability initiative to Vietnam. The collaboration has already established traceable soybean and soybean meal supply chains from Brazil to Thailand.

THAILAND

Thai police arrest Pattaya crypto investment-scam suspects

Thai police have arrested four foreign nationals in Pattaya over an alleged scam that defrauded victims of more than 400 million baht ($11.8M) through fake crypto investments.

The operation followed the rescue of a 19-year-old Chinese student held for ransom three days earlier and uncovered a crypto romance scam allegedly run by three Chinese nationals and one Taiwanese fugitive.

title: Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future
On November 10, 2026, President Nayib Bukele hosted roughly 30 Bitcoiners at Casa Presidencial during Bitcoin Histórico. Guests included Ricardo Salinas Pliego, Parker Lewis, ...
content:
This November 10, in the midst of the Bitcoin Histórico conference taking place in the Historical Center of San Salvador, a group of Bitcoiners representing a wide range of sectors within the industry met with President Bukele.

The dinner was organized by The Bitcoin Office, which is part of the Office of the President, and was led by Stacy Herbert and Max Keiser. The dinner went on from about 7:30 pm to 10:30 pm local time and included about thirty Bitcoiners, many regular visitors to El Salvador. 

Among the guests was billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego, founder of Grupo Salinas, which owns Banco Azteca. Salinas is a known Bitcoiner, who has made public appearances with Keiser and Herbert in the past, and is speculated to be planning a run at the next Mexican Presidential election. Salinas met privately with the President besides the dinner and reportedly gifted him volumes one and two of Manuscripts of the Conquistadors, works curated and edited by Jorge Nikaido, Chief of Staff of Grupo Salinas.

Representing investors and founders were Parker Lewis, founder of Unchained Capital, Mike Peterson of Bitcoin Beach fame, Katie Ananina of Citizen X, and Aleks Svetski, entrepreneur and founder of Satlantis. Bitcoin miners also attended, such as  Beau Turner,  CEO of  Abundant Mines, Nacho Pauls, CCO of OCEAN Mining, and Adam Ortolf of Denver Bitcoin mining. Jon Atack, a Bitcoin core contributor, was also at the dinner alongside engineer Giacomo Zucco of Plan B Network, and AI tech entrepreneurs Ginger Gaetz of the ANIA AI initiative and Marc Seal, Founder of Aevonix.

The academic and media side of the industry was also heavily represented, with none other than Michael Goldstein, also known as Bitstein and co-founder of the Nakamoto Institute. Eric Yakes, economist and author of The 7th Property, was there, as well as Efrat Feningson, independent journalist and podcaster. Local Bitcoiner Michael Ruiz also attended the dinner; he is the founder of Build in El Salvador (BIS), an increasingly popular kind of business club and Bitcoin meetup mix. 

Setting the Table

The guests arrived at the Casa Presidencial earlier in the evening and were chatting and networking while waiting for the president. Max Keiser, always a showman, arrived at the Casa Presidencial with a gift some might speculate carried a magical artefact. Photographed above, the case was said to contain a Stetson El Presidente cowboy hat, though some have speculated it might in fact have carried the Philosopher’s Stone. 

Upon arrival, Bukele shook everyone’s hand and quickly invited them to take their assigned seats, dine, and relax- no big speeches or over-the-top formalities, Ananina told Bitcoin Magazine, describing the dinner as a kind of open mic. 

“President Bukele’s table was adorned with bitcoin orange florals,” Herbert told Bitcoin Magazine; “we gathered anarchists, billionaire tycoons, Wall Street bankers, circular economy activists, VC investors, bitcoin miners, and content creators” at the country’s equivalent of the White House.  

A three-course meal began to be served, with steak — of course — being the main course, followed by a three-layered chocolate dessert. In between were three hours of conversation which left a very strong impression on the individuals interviewed on the night. Bukele had his own microphone, while a couple of other mics were passed around. Six to seven major questions were asked throughout the night.

Salinas and Energy Investments

At some point, energy generation came up, and Salinas in particular engaged the topic with the President. 

Baeu Turner, one of the three bitcoin miners at the dinner, told Bitcoin Magazine that Bukele described El Salvador’s electricity generation as “being roughly matched to the country’s current demand.” Bukele described plans to add more than a gigawatt of additional generation across multiple projects, including geothermal and generation using imported liquefied natural gas.

“What stood out to me,” added Turner, “was how directly he connected those development plans with demand for compute. Bukele said they can develop this power knowing there are users who can put it to work, whether that’s Bitcoin mining or other data centers. The demand could come from the Salvadoran government’s own operations or from outside companies bringing equipment and investment into the country.”

Other miners responded positively to that idea, including Salinas, who has deep investments and experience with energy production. His Grupo Dragón is involved in geothermal, wind, solar, and natural-gas generation across Mexico. 

Immigration and Gentrification

Immigration was also discussed. Spurred by Max Keiser’s enthusiasm about the country, where he roughly said that the world should recognize El Salvador’s arc and that people — bitcoiners presumably — should migrate; suddenly the topic was set on the table. Ruiz, whose family is from the region but was born and raised in the U.S., moved to El Salvador three years ago and has become a recognizable figure in the local Bitcoin community. He followed up with a question about immigration, in particular about gentrification and possible resentment from the local population towards Western migrants, pointing to very negative online comments about some Bitcoiners, such as being called “colonizers”.

Bukele asked back, “When you go out, walk around, and interact with Salvadorans, what are the interactions like?”, The question, to anyone that’s spent time in El Salvador in recent years, answers itself. Salvadorians are very welcoming, Ruiz told Bitcoin Magazine; “there’s a lot of love. People receive us with open arms, and they’re glad we’re here, and they’re happy”. 

Immigration in El Salvador actually tends to be from regional countries like Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala, and Colombia, with smaller numbers reported from the United States. Bukele went on to dismiss concerns about immigration, joking that you could host the whole population of the world in El Salvador by matching the population density of Manhattan. This was not a statement meant to be taken as a goal or ideal, but rather to set the topic in context. He added that the country is obviously looking for the most capable and intelligent people, and even said that “all great empires were built with immigrants’ help”, which says a lot about the President’s mindset on the topic.

In response to concerns about gentrification, the President told the story of a fisherman and house caretaker who got a raise from $300 to $800 a month from an American who bought the property. As a result, the fisherman was able to buy a motor for his boat, which he used to fish and row by hand before that. The scale-up of his fishing business was so productive that the caretaker even got his son a boat, doubling his fishing fleet. The only people who complained about this growth in wages were the neighbours, so the story goes, who must have been feeling the pressure from their own villa’s caretakers, wanting a raise from meager wages. 

Among other Topics

At some point Efrat asked, “How come you are criticized around the world despite El Salvador’s GDP growth, a strengthening economy and popularity at home, which I saw firsthand talking to locals and visiting some of the areas once worst hit by gang violence?”

“Because I’m not part of their club,” the President allegedly responded, “I’m not the kind of ruler they like”. He added that there are evil people in the world who use mainstream media to criticize leaders like him and “call him names”, central bankers, including the ECB, came up as one of the forces behind the negative media campaign against Bukele.

Beyond the clear hit pieces, he noted that many people in governments or the international political establishment are not evil per se, but are often ‘order followers’, who operate on certain narratives and resist new paradigms. 

The recent wins for the country in terms of education reform were also discussed. Bukele allegedly said that many private schools are now integrating similar AI tutoring programs as the one led by his administration. The results made international news when the pilot program deployed in public schools over the past couple of years brought PISA test results to par with Germany and Switzerland.

Renaissance 2.0

When asked about their reflections on the presidential dinner and the Bitcoin Histórico conference in general, Max Kaiser shared his vision in a manner that merits being printed in full:

“Bitcoin Histórico promised two days of Excellence Only, as the Bitcoin Office likes to say, and it delivered big time. The National Palace was a regal setting to showcase the Renaissance 2.0 taking shape in El Salvador with presentations by the best Bitcoin minds and builders in the world. Audience members felt like they had been transported to a time and place found nowhere else in the world right now, where hope and happiness are in abundance. No doom.”

Stacy Herbert, whose presence and attention to detail were felt throughout the festivities, told Bitcoin Magazine, “We promoted Bitcoin Histórico as an elevated bitcoin conference experience with Philosopher King meets Renaissance 2.0 vibes. In every detail, my team and I achieved that, including with the official Bitcoin Office dinner at Casa Presidencial.” She added that guests were free to ask any question they wanted, and that no topic was off limits. 

“They grilled the President for several hours. His wit, his charm, his intelligence – all unscripted – was there for all to see firsthand. And they will have walked away understanding why it is that El Salvador is winning under his leadership.” Herbert added. As far as attendees to the dinner who Bitcoin Magazine spoke with, both claims remain very much corroborated.

title: Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides
Strategy shares fell 4.6% to $86.13 on Thursday, their sixth straight decline, as bitcoin dipped below $62,000. The company's 850,849 BTC are now worth about $11 billion less than it paid.
This post Strat...
content:
Strategy (MSTR) shares fell 4.6% on Thursday to close at $86.13, their sixth straight daily decline, as bitcoin dipped below $62,000 and a broad selloff hit U.S. stocks. In after hours trading, shares were down to $85.50.

The stock opened near $93 and slid through the afternoon, finishing near its low of about $86. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped more than 1,000 points, and the Nasdaq Composite lost about 2.1%. Bitcoin touched a low of $61,658 during the session, its weakest price since July. It was back near $62,000 late in the afternoon.

Strategy stock extends its slide

The drop adds to a brutal month for the largest corporate holder of bitcoin. Strategy shares are down about 37% from their $136.02 close on Oct. 19, and down about 29% from the $121.07 close on Nov. 10, which is when the latest leg lower began. Thursday was the stock’s sixth consecutive losing session.

The slide has wiped out most of the year’s value. Strategy closed 2025 at $151.95, which puts the stock down about 43% in 2026. The shares fell below $100 on Tuesday and now trade about 11% below Tuesday’s $96.50 close. That day they also dipped under the company’s STRC preferred for the first time since mid-August.

Thursday’s move tracked bitcoin closely. Institutions have kept buying even so, and a New York state pension fund boosted its stake by more than 10% in a recent filing. The bitcoin price slumped under $62,000 as traders weighed the risk of Federal Reserve rate hikes and a sharp pullback in technology stocks.

Holdings now sit well below cost

Strategy added 485 bitcoin in the week ending Nov. 15, according to its Nov. 16 Form 8-K. It paid $33.4 million, or an average of $68,887 per coin, and its total reached 850,849 BTC.

Those coins cost $64.20 billion, or an average of $75,452 each. With bitcoin near $62,000, the stack is worth roughly $52.8 billion, which leaves Strategy with an unrealized loss of about $11 billion. Bitcoin is trading about 18% below the company’s average purchase price.

The 850,849 coins are more than 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap, and the company also held about $4.9 billion in U.S. dollar reserves as of Nov. 15, which gives it a cushion for preferred dividends and buybacks. Strategy has not announced a new purchase since that filing. It has reported its buys on Mondays in recent weeks, so the next update would normally come Monday.

Preferred buybacks take priority

Most of Strategy’s recent cash has gone to its preferred stock instead of bitcoin. In the same filing, the company said it repurchased 2,282,510 shares of its STRC preferred for $228.1 million, nearly seven times what it spent on bitcoin.

It funded the purchases with $244.7 million raised from selling common stock. The 8-K shows $332.2 million remaining under the preferred repurchase program and $1.0 billion under its common stock buyback authorization.

Executive Chairman Michael Saylor said on X that Strategy plans to keep going. He wrote that STRC traded more than $600 million on Wednesday, calling it the only one of 456 U.S.-listed income preferreds to do so this year.

He said the buybacks add liquidity, lower dividend obligations and strengthen the credit. “We intend to keep buying below $100,” Saylor wrote.

title: SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam
The SEC charged eight Colorado-based entities, likely run from overseas, with taking more than $37 million from U.S. investors through fake advisers, fake crypto trading platforms and fake SEC certificates.
T...
content:
The SEC charged eight Colorado-based entities on Thursday with running a fake investment adviser and crypto trading platform scheme that took more than $37 million from U.S. investors. The agency said the defendants are likely operated by people overseas.

According to the SEC’s complaint, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, the defendants defrauded more than 1,500 investors from at least August 2024 through May 2026. The advisers and the trading platforms they pointed victims to were fronts, the agency alleged, and none of the crypto assets investors thought they were buying existed.

How the scheme worked

Social media ads sent prospective victims to WhatsApp group and private chats run by the scammers. People in those chats posing as investment advisers first gave advice on trading U.S. stocks, then pushed victims to send as much money as possible to a supposed crypto trading platform.

The complaint says the scheme ran in four adviser and platform pairs, each active for roughly six months. Advisor WeChat Capital and Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance operated from about August to December 2024. HB Wealth Advisors and IdeaCrypto Exchange followed from January to July 2025.

Convergent Wealth Advisors and RealSimple Crypto Exchange ran from about July to December 2025. Associated Wealth Advisors and Essential Crypto Exchange closed out the scheme from January to May 2026. Each pair vanished after collecting millions, the SEC said, and a new one took its place.

Victims were told to buy ether, tether or USDC on a U.S. exchange and move it to a self-custody wallet. They then sent it to an address supplied by the adviser, and a realistic app showed balances and gains that were invented.

When investors tried to withdraw their supposed profits, they were told they first had to pay a fee, calculated as a percentage of those profits, in crypto to a separate address. The complaint says investors who balked were threatened and pressured. Eventually the websites went down and the chats went silent.

Fake certificates and real losses

To look legitimate, the defendants made fake SEC certificates and pointed skeptical investors to real filings with the SEC, FINRA and FinCEN. The complaint says those filings carry no regulatory approval, since registering for access to its EDGAR system is ministerial and Forms ADV are not reviewed before publication.

The complaint says Convergent Wealth and Essential Crypto also filed false Forms ADV listing regulatory contacts who do not appear to be real and offices in Colorado that did not exist. The SEC said a Form D and the two Forms ADV have been removed from its website.

Three unnamed investors illustrate the damage. One lost nearly $500,000, including money borrowed from a 401(k), a son and a neighbor. Another lost about $850,000, partly by liquidating a 401(k), and a third lost close to $1.6 million, including the investor’s house and IRA.

Charges and what the SEC wants

All eight entities face charges under Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5. The four advisers are also charged under Sections 206(1) and 206(2) of the Investment Advisers Act, and Convergent Wealth and Essential Crypto face an additional charge under Section 207.

The SEC is seeking permanent injunctions, disgorgement of ill-gotten gains with prejudgment interest, and civil penalties. It also wants the advisers barred from acting as or being associated with any investment adviser, and Convergent Wealth and Essential Crypto barred from filing as exempt reporting advisers.

The agency thanked regulators in Hong Kong, Singapore, mainland China and Switzerland for their help. It also pointed to its investor alerts on group chats and on false claims of SEC registration, and urged investors to check the background of anyone selling them an investment at Investor.gov.

“The SEC continues to seek out and expose fraudulent investment scams that prey on U.S. investors,” said Laura D’Allaird, chief of the SEC Enforcement Division’s Cyber and Emerging Technologies Unit.

title: A New Recovery Model? Binance Wins $6.5B Freezing Order Across 26K Wallets
summary: Binance has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order from Abu Dhabi’s ADGM Courts as it pursues assets stolen in the Oct. 29 hack. The ruling introduces an unusual weapon for crypto recovery: a constantly updated list of 26,000 wallets that can be served and tracked through the blockchain.   ...
content:
Binance has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order from Abu Dhabi’s ADGM Courts as it pursues assets stolen in the Oct. 29 hack. The ruling introduces an unusual weapon for crypto recovery: a constantly updated list of 26,000 wallets that can be served and tracked through the blockchain.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance has secured a $6.5B global freeze order covering 26,000 wallets tied to the Oct. 29 hack.
  • Approximately $2.85B has already been frozen or seized by stablecoin issuers and exchanges.
  • The 26,000-wallet living list could become a model for tracing and recovering stolen crypto.

Abu Dhabi Court Grants Binance $6.5B Global Crypto Freeze

Binance has turned to an Abu Dhabi court for one of the largest asset-freezing orders ever sought in crypto.

The exchange obtained a $6.5 billion worldwide injunction against unidentified perpetrators of its Oct. 29 security breach, according to a Bloomberg report. The FBI has attributed the roughly $6.3 billion theft to North Korea’s Tradertraitor group.

The $6.5 billion figure represents assets covered by the injunction. It does not mean that amount has already been frozen or recovered.

Court Order Follows the Crypto Across 26,000 Wallets

The most significant feature may be how the order operates.

Binance’s lawyers identified a “living list” of 26,000 wallet addresses linked to stolen assets. The list can be updated as funds move, while the court orders can be served through the blockchain, allowing exchanges, issuers, and other market participants to react faster.

The court also granted proprietary injunctions and delivery-up orders covering specific assets, including funds held by parties that Binance does not accuse of wrongdoing.

“We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze, and recover stolen assets,” Binance Deputy General Counsel Dugan Bliss said.

Nearly $2.85 Billion Has Already Been Immobilized

Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic has verified about $2.85 billion in frozen or seized assets, roughly 44% of the theft. Most were stablecoins whose issuers could block movement.

The U.S. Justice Department separately secured authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion connected to the Binance hack.

Binance says affected customer assets have already been replenished and users absorbed no losses.

The larger implication reaches beyond one exchange. Crypto thieves can move assets between thousands of addresses at machine speed. The ADGM ruling shows courts are beginning to adapt in kind, using blockchain itself to deliver legal orders and follow stolen funds as they move.

If that approach proves effective, then the 26,000-wallet list could become a blueprint for recovering crypto after major hacks.

title: Bitcoin Price Slumps Under $62,000, Crashing 25% in One Month
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slumps Under $62,000, Crashing 25% in One Month
The bitcoin price slumped under $62,000 on Thursday, down about 24% in one month, as Anthropic's Nasdaq debut set off a tech selloff that hit crypto stocks.
This post Bitcoin Price Slumps Under $62,000, Crashing 25% in O...
content:
The bitcoin price slumped under $62,000 on Thursday afternoon, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, extending a slide of about 24% in one month as Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut set off a broad selloff in tech stocks.

Bitcoin was trading near $81,800 on Oct. 19. It touched a low of about $61,650 on Thursday, its weakest level since July, before steadying near $62,200. The drop was about 25% from the Oct. 19 close, based on daily data.

The slide came in steps. Bitcoin closed near $80,050 on Oct. 25, about $78,250 on Nov. 1 and about $74,750 on Nov. 8. The steepest leg came last week, when it fell about 12.6% to a Nov. 15 close near $65,300, and the losses have continued this week.

Bitcoin had climbed back to about $64,000 early Thursday as Anthropic’s record IPO lifted stock futures, as this morning’s report showed. The rally faded once U.S. markets opened. The bitcoin price fell from roughly $63,900 at the opening bell to about $62,200 by midday.

Anthropic debut sparks a tech selloff

Anthropic shares opened shortly before noon at $111.50, 34% above the $83 IPO price, CNBC reported. The opening trade valued the Claude maker at more than $2 trillion. The stock quickly pulled back and was last near $97, about 17% above its offering price.

The broader market went the other way. The major averages fell to session lows soon after Anthropic began trading, as investors took profits on the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite dropped about 2% after gaining as much as 2% earlier in the session, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost about 1,000 points.

Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, told CNBC the premarket rally had faded even before Anthropic began trading. He called it the latest round of “sell the rally” trading. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 3%, and the S&P 500 headed toward a sixth straight loss, the AP reported.

The Cboe Volatility Index, Wall Street’s fear gauge, climbed to about 28 after touching nearly 29 shortly after Anthropic began trading. That was its highest level since March, up from about 24.6 at Wednesday’s close. The bitcoin price moved in step with the Nasdaq through the afternoon.

Crypto stocks erase their morning gains

Crypto stocks followed the Nasdaq lower in late-afternoon trading, about 3:55 p.m. ET. Strategy (MSTR) traded near $86.70, down about 4% on the day. Galaxy Digital (GLXY) dropped about 6.9%, the steepest decline in the group.

Coinbase (COIN) slipped about 0.9% to near $109.50, while Circle (CRCL) fell about 2.2%. Bitcoin miners gave back their early rally too. IREN (IREN) fell about 5.6%, CleanSpark (CLSK) lost about 5.4% and MARA Holdings (MARA) declined about 4.2%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) was down about 2.9%.

Fed hike risk keeps pressure on the bitcoin price

The Fed remains a headwind. Bets on a December rate hike have grown after minutes from the October meeting showed more policymakers backing higher rates, and some officials called for a half-point move.

The bitcoin price is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, which would be its second-longest losing streak after nine weeks of declines in 2022. The streak has erased roughly $20,000 from the bitcoin price since mid-October, based on daily closes. Bitcoin price hit its weakest level since July on Thursday, and the Fed meets again next month.

Longer-term holders have not left. Institutional investors added 49,229 BTC through U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter, lifting their holdings to a record 356,491 BTC. Swiss bank Sygnum called the current downturn the shallowest bear market to date and sees a path to a new high near $128,000.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,900.

title: MoonPay seeks US bank charter for stablecoin, custody services
summary: MoonPay’s proposed national trust bank would offer stablecoin issuance and redemption, reserve management and digital asset custody under federal oversight.
content:
Crypto payments firm MoonPay has applied for a US national trust bank charter to offer stablecoin issuance and redemption, reserve management and digital asset custody services.

According to an OCC filing, MoonPay submitted its application on Tuesday to establish MoonPay National Trust Bank, a non-depository institution headquartered in Miami Beach, Florida. The proposed bank would not accept traditional deposits or issue loans.

MoonPay already provides stablecoin issuance infrastructure to businesses, including support for branded digital dollars. If approved, the charter would allow its proposed banking subsidiary to provide stablecoin and custody services under federal supervision.

The application comes as US regulators prepare to implement the GENIUS Act, which takes effect on Jan. 18, 2027, and establishes federal standards for stablecoin issuers, including reserve backing and redemption requirements.

With the filing, MoonPay joins several crypto and payments companies seeking federal trust bank charters, including Rain, Modern Treasury and Block. Coinbase’s charter took effect earlier this month, while Circle received final OCC approval in July.

The rise in crypto firms applying for federal trust bank charters has drawn opposition from community banks. In October, the Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC, arguing that the regulator exceeded its authority by allowing non-depository trust banks to conduct activities traditionally associated with commercial banks.

title: Hyperliquid Anthropic futures priced within 1% of Nasdaq opening price
summary: Hyperliquid traders priced Anthropic futures within 1% of the stock’s Nasdaq opening price, as trading surged ahead of the AI company’s IPO.
content:
Anthropic perpetual futures on Hyperliquid were priced within 1% of the company’s Nasdaq opening share price Thursday, shortly before the stock began trading.

Anthropic shares opened at $111.50, up 34.3% from the company’s $83 initial public offering (IPO) price, according to several data dashboards. The opening price valued the Claude AI chatbot maker at around $2 trillion.

Just before trading began, Anthropic futures on Hyperliquid’s trade.xyz market were priced at $110.48, according to Senpi at around 4:44 pm UTC. That was just $1.02, or 0.91%, below the stock’s opening price.

The massive debut once again puts crypto’s growing pre-IPO futures market in the spotlight, especially as exchanges compete to attract traders who want to bet on major companies before their shares begin trading on Wall Street. SpaceX’s debut earlier this year also drew interest from crypto traders betting on its stock price through crypto futures.

Perpetual futures allow traders to bet on whether prices will rise or fall without owning the underlying shares, and unlike traditional futures they have no expiration date and can trade around the clock — including before a company goes public.

Anthropic trading accelerates on Hyperliquid

Trading on Hyperliquid was especially strong just before Anthropic shares opened, with the contract on trade.xyz recording $545.7 million in trading volume over 24 hours and $303.3 million in open interest (OI), according to Senpi data.

The contract was also trading at a 2.58% premium to its oracle price, the same data showed.

This interest had been growing for weeks, according to a Thursday report from crypto research firm Block Scholes, which found that daily trading volume for Anthropic futures on Hyperliquid averaged $75 million since Nov. 5, up from $7 million in September.

Traders also appeared to be betting on Anthropic’s stock rising, according to Token Terminal data, which showed that 5,567 traders held long positions in Anthropic futures on Hyperliquid on Wednesday, compared with 1,996 holding short positions.

Open interest in Anthropic perpetual futures on Hyperliquid reached a record $186 million on Nov. 18. Source: Token Terminal

OI across Anthropic futures markets on Hyperliquid also reached a record $186 million on Wednesday. Of that, $86 million came from trade.xyz contracts, while Entropy.io accounted for about $100 million.

Still, Anthropic futures made up just 1% of Hyperliquid’s total trading volume and accounted for only 3% of the increase in non-crypto trading since September, the Block Scholes report found.

Related: SpaceX tokenized IPO campaign draws $557M on Binance ahead of debut

Binance leads Anthropic futures volume

Binance recorded about $741 million in Anthropic perpetual futures trading over 24 hours, compared with $195 million on OKX, according to DefiLlama. Entropy’s Anthropic market, which also runs on Hyperliquid, recorded about $80 million.

Those three exchanges recorded $214 million, $34 million and $110 million in OI, respectively. Across 15 Anthropic perpetual futures markets, OI came in at a combined $520.4 million as of 4:50 pm UTC.

Anthropic shares were trading at $98.49 as of 5:43 pm UTC on Thursday, down about 12% from their $111.50 opening price but still nearly 19% above the $83 IPO price.

Anthropic joins Saudi Aramco and SpaceX as one of just three companies to debut on public markets with a trillion-dollar valuation.

title: Trump Media’s $883M Debt Deadline Puts Bitcoin Holdings in Focus
summary: Trump Media and Technology Group repurchased $100 million of its convertible debt at a discount, reducing its outstanding obligations to approximately $883.5 million ahead of a Nov. 30 repayment deadline. Trump Media Cuts Debt Ahead of Repayment Deadline Trump Media and Technology Group (TMTG) has r...
content:
Trump Media and Technology Group repurchased $100 million of its convertible debt at a discount, reducing its outstanding obligations to approximately $883.5 million ahead of a Nov. 30 repayment deadline.

Key Takeaways

  • Trump Media repurchased $100M in convertible notes at a discount, cutting its remaining debt to $883.5M.
  • With its stock trading near $4, investors are likely to reject conversion, forcing Trump Media to cover a $393M cash gap.
  • Trump Media may sell part of its 15,649 Bitcoin stash if credit deals fail before the Nov. 30 deadline.

Trump Media Cuts Debt Ahead of Repayment Deadline

Trump Media and Technology Group (TMTG) has repurchased $100 million in principal amount of its 0% convertible senior secured notes due May 29, 2028. The transaction, disclosed Nov. 17, 2026, was executed at a discount to face value using cash on hand, reducing the company’s outstanding principal by slightly more than 10% to approximately $883.5 million.

The buyback comes less than two weeks before a critical financial deadline for the company. Under the terms of the notes, originally issued in May 2025 to fund a corporate bitcoin treasury, noteholders have a one-time put option allowing them to demand full cash repayment at face value on Nov. 30, 2026.

“Our robust balance sheet gives us the flexibility we need to address our bond obligations,” said Kevin McGurn, TMTG’s interim CEO, in a statement. “As I said on our recent earnings call, we intend to use available cash and credit to clean up our capital structure, without issuing any additional equity, and yesterday’s repurchase is one part of that strategy.”

While the discounted buyback reduces TMTG’s outstanding debt, attention is turning to how the Truth Social parent company will cover the remaining $883.5 million if bondholders exercise their Nov. 30 put rights. The notes carry a conversion price of approximately $34.72 per share. With the shares having fallen 69% so far in 2026 and recently trading near $4 per share, converting the debt into stock is significantly less attractive to bondholders than demanding cash repayment.

McGurn had said on the earlier earnings call that Trump Media hoped to “preserve as much of our bitcoin as possible to continue our yield strategy and allow that asset to recover.”

Bitcoin Reserves Face Potential Liquidation Risk

According to TMTG’s most recent quarterly filings for the period ended Sept. 30, 2026, the company held approximately $393 million in cash and short-term investments. With those reserves falling well short of the $883.5 million maximum potential payout, TMTG faces a substantial liquidity gap if most noteholders demand repayment.

Nevertheless, TMTG management has emphasized its intention to use existing cash and new credit facilities rather than issue additional shares or liquidate its cryptocurrency reserves. As of Sept. 30, TMTG held approximately 15,649 bitcoin (BTC)—about $970 million worth—including 4,261 BTC pledged as collateral securing the notes.

Despite McGurn’s preference to retain the bitcoin until prices recover, TMTG acknowledged in its third-quarter regulatory filings that if refinancing efforts or credit arrangements prove insufficient, the company could be forced to sell bitcoin, seek additional borrowing or raise equity on unfavorable terms.

Meanwhile, TMTG said its board has authorized the company to continue repurchasing additional notes from time to time, both before and after the Nov. 30 deadline.

title: Trump’s SEC nominee Johnson backs formal rulemaking for tokenized stock trading
summary: Former CFTC Commissioner and Democrat Kristin Johnson and ex-SEC aide Steven Levine appeared before lawmakers Thursday.
content:
President Donald Trump’s nominees to fill two vacancies at the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) faced questions about investor protections, regulatory oversight and financial innovation during a Senate confirmation hearing Thursday, including scrutiny of the agency’s approach to tokenized securities.

Kristin Johnson, Trump’s Democratic nominee, backed formal rulemaking to address concerns about the agency’s exemption for tokenized stock trading.

“I feel strongly that regulation is made better through the notice and comment period,” Johnson told the Senate Banking Committee in response to Democratic Senator Angela Alsobrooks. She added that she would welcome the opportunity to address issues covered by the exemption through that process.

The SEC’s Sept. 17 exemption lets qualifying platforms trade blockchain-based versions of US-listed shares without registering as securities exchanges under certain conditions. The order took effect immediately and invites comments on possible changes.

Johnson, a former Commodity Futures Trading Commission commissioner, appeared alongside Republican Steven Levine, a former aide to SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda. If confirmed, they would bring the five-member commission to four members, with three Republicans and one Democrat.

The hearing comes as the SEC has scaled back enforcement activity and pursued regulatory changes intended to accommodate digital assets, including efforts to facilitate tokenized securities that have drawn scrutiny from lawmakers and market participants.

Companies reject tokenized stock listings

The measure has drawn objections from publicly traded companies, with 67 opposing the tokenization of their shares on the OKXICE platform, according to a Nov. 5 public notice.

Johnson also cited concerns about Anti-Money Laundering and Know Your Customer compliance, noting that objections to the exemption extended beyond investor protection.

Levine, meanwhile, said he had not closely studied the innovation exemption but understood it to be time-limited and include investor protections. He emphasized that Congress had authorized the SEC to grant exemptions from federal securities laws when doing so serves the public interest and remains consistent with investor protection requirements.

He pointed to exchange-traded funds as an example of financial innovation that initially developed through regulatory exemptions before becoming subject to broader agency rules.

Related: Robinhood’s Tenev warns US tokenization uncertainty deters ‘serious assets’

Senate weighs bipartisan SEC appointments

If confirmed, Johnson would become the SEC’s only Democratic commissioner, a development some in the crypto industry believe could strengthen the agency’s approach to regulation.

“Crypto isn’t a partisan issue, and the rules that come out of a bipartisan commission will stand on firmer footing,” Jessica Martinez, US policy director at digital asset infrastructure company Fireblocks, told Cointelegraph.

Martinez added that even minority commissioners can influence policy by challenging proposals and pushing for unresolved issues to be addressed before rules are finalized.

Senators have until noon Friday to submit additional written questions to the nominees, with responses due by 5:00 pm ET on Nov. 24, according to the committee’s closing remarks.

The nominations could then advance to a committee vote before being considered by the full Senate. Both nominees would require Senate confirmation before taking their seats at the SEC.

title: Institutions are Piling Into Bitcoin ETFs, Pushing Holdings to a Record
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Institutions are Piling Into Bitcoin ETFs, Pushing Holdings to a Record
Galaxy Research says 13F filers added 49,229 BTC through U.S. spot bitcoin ETPs in Q3, lifting institutional holdings to a record 356,491 BTC as Wells Fargo became the largest holder.
This post Institutions are...
content:
Institutions returned to U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded products as net buyers in the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record 356,491 BTC, according to a new report from Galaxy Research.

Investment managers that file Form 13F with the SEC added the equivalent o f 49,229 BTC, net of sales, between July 1 and Sept. 30. That is the most since the second quarter of 2025 and more than the 47,054 BTC they sold over the previous three quarters. The holdings were worth $29.78 billion at quarter-end prices.

Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, published the analysis Thursday. The buying came as bitcoin swung between a bear-market low of $57,717 on July 1 and a high of $87,397 on Sept. 21, and Galaxy said the accumulation continued through that range.

Wealth platforms lead the buying

Half of the net addition came from advisors and wealth platforms, a group that includes registered investment advisors, wealth managers, wirehouses and broker-dealer platforms. The category reported 144,307 BTC, or 40.5% of all 13F-reported holdings, the highest share since the funds launched in January 2024.

Those firms have now been net buyers for nine straight quarters. Their holdings are 3.3 times their March 2024 level, and Galaxy said the group accounts for 100,003 of the 179,300 BTC that all filers have added since the second quarter of 2024.

Wirehouses drove the quarter. The category added a record 24,838 BTC, led by Wells Fargo at 14,636 BTC, Bank of America at 7,201 BTC and Morgan Stanley at 2,875 BTC.

Wells Fargo became the largest 13F holder for the first time. It reported 30,553 BTC, worth $2.55 billion, nearly double the 15,931 BTC it held on June 30, and passed Jane Street. No wealth platform had ranked first before, and Millennium Management had held the top spot in every quarter from early 2024 through the first quarter of 2026.

Hedge funds step back, IBIT dominates

Hedge funds now hold 19.0% of 13F-reported holdings, down from 50.6% at the end of 2024. Basis and relative-value funds hold 34,053 BTC, far below their peak of 101,826 BTC, though they and macro funds were both buyers last quarter, adding 9,184 BTC and 10,492 BTC.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounts for two-thirds of the institutional position. Filers hold 232,453 BTC in the fund, or 65.2% of everything reported, and IBIT took 34,744 BTC of the quarter’s net 49,229 BTC.

Filers’ holdings of Grayscale’s GBTC fell for the 10th straight quarter, and the lower-fee Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust passed it for the first time. The number of managers holding a spot bitcoin fund rose by 191 to 2,166, the first increase after two quarters of decline.

Galaxy noted that a few large firms drove the gain. The 50 largest holders added a net 59,578 BTC, while all other managers combined were net sellers of 10,349 BTC. Form 13F filers hold 27.6% of the bitcoin in the funds, up from 24.8% on June 30.

A snapshot that has already aged

The filings describe Sept. 30, and the picture has changed since. Galaxy said the funds’ bitcoin holdings have fallen by 38,531 BTC to 1,252,139 BTC as of Nov. 16, while the price of bitcoin dropped to $64,943 from $83,580. Bitcoin had traded above $81,500 as recently as Oct. 28.

A Form 13F covers only long positions at quarter-end and only accounts over which the manager has investment discretion. Short positions and most derivatives are not reported, so shares held by a market maker or basis fund may be hedged. Galaxy also believes client-directed brokerage accounts leave wealth-channel ownership understated.

How filers behaved during the recent decline will not be known until the next round of filings arrives in February.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin Giant Strategy Will Keep Buying STRC Below $100 After $600M Day: Saylor
summary: Michael Saylor said Strategy’s STRC preferred shares exceeded $600 million in trading as the stock fell 2.62% on Nov. 18. He reiterated the bitcoin treasury leader’s intention to repurchase shares below $100. Saylor Highlights a $600 Million Trading Day Michael Saylor, Strategy’s founder and executi...
content:
Michael Saylor said Strategy’s STRC preferred shares exceeded $600 million in trading as the stock fell 2.62% on Nov. 18. He reiterated the bitcoin treasury leader’s intention to repurchase shares below $100.

Key Takeaways

  • Strategy’s STRC recorded more than $600 million in trading on Nov. 18 as shares fell in price.
  • STRC closed below the $100 stated amount used to set its dividends.
  • The company spent $228.1 million repurchasing STRC in the prior week.

Saylor Highlights a $600 Million Trading Day

Michael Saylor, Strategy’s founder and executive chairman, reported more than $600 million in STRC trading on Nov. 19 for the previous day. He described it as the only one of 456 U.S.-listed income preferred stocks to reach that level this year.

Nov. 18 trading ran more than three times STRC’s 30-day average of $198.6 million, according to Strategy’s STRC trading figures. The stock closed at $96.11, down 2.62% for the day and $3.89 below its $100 stated amount. The $100 stated amount is used to calculate dividends; it does not guarantee a $100 trading price.

Saylor wrote on X:

“We intend to keep buying below $100.”

Repurchases Retire Future Dividend Claims

Strategy repurchased 2,282,510 STRC shares for $228.1 million during Nov. 9-15, a Nov. 16 filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) showed. Proceeds from sales of MSTR common shares funded $206.3 million of those purchases, while interest earned on dollar assets covered the other $21.8 million. The filing listed $332.2 million still available under its preferred securities repurchase program.

Buying STRC below $100 can retire preferred shares, along with the dividends they would have paid, for less than their stated amount, Saylor explained. That can reduce payment obligations, although the company spends cash or raises funds to buy the shares. He characterized buybacks as discretionary rather than a guaranteed price floor.

That week, Strategy directed more money to STRC than bitcoin. It acquired 485 BTC for $33.4 million during Nov. 9-15 while spending $228.1 million on preferred-share repurchases. Both transactions occurred before the Nov. 18 surge in trading and price decline.

The $100 Target and Shareholder Trade-Off

The balance between STRC repurchases and bitcoin purchases has shifted. In late October, Strategy spent $204.9 million on STRC repurchases during a week when it bought no bitcoin, drawing on cash available for broader treasury operations rather than its designated dividend reserve.

For December, Strategy maintained STRC’s 12% annual dividend rate, leaving its payout unchanged as the share price moved below its $100 stated amount. At that rate, each share repurchased removes $12 in annual dividend obligations if the rate remains unchanged.

As the price of bitcoin declined, Saylor compared STRC’s dividend-inclusive returns with the cryptocurrency’s performance. In his Nov. 19 X post, Saylor argued that the company believes repurchases “strengthen the credit and benefit common shareholders.” Issuing MSTR shares to fund those repurchases spreads ownership across more common shares, diluting existing holders’ percentage stakes.

Securities issued by bitcoin treasury companies carry corporate financing and management risks distinct from owning bitcoin directly. Strategy’s latest filing reported a $4.75 billion reserve designated for preferred dividends and debt interest as of Nov. 15, alongside $151.2 million in separate cash available for broader treasury purposes.

Solana’s tokens now surpass the billion-dollar mark as it establishes a foothold in the real-world asset (RWA) market. Solana said circulating value reached $1.22 billion, nearly doubling from the level recorded at the end of October.

$1.22B in circulating value, nearly double where October closed. https://t.co/d7T8UgQIfM

  • Tokenized Equities Cross $1 Billion on Solana
  • Ondo and Securitize Expand the Onchain Stock Market
    • More Traditional Securities Are Moving Onchain
  • DTCC Plans Solana Integration for 2027

Tokenized Equities Cross $1 Billion on Solana

On Nov. 19, Solana revealed the milestone, reporting that tokenization of equity supply surged in November.

The figure is of the value of the tokens circulating and not of the total volume of trading they produced. That’s important because trades occurring at sites like xStocks and Backpack are already reaching billions of dollars.

Solana’s October ecosystem report indicated that xStocks have accumulated $7.5 billion in trading volume and tokenized assets available via Backpaks Securities surpassed $6 billion in trading volume.

Ondo and Securitize Expand the Onchain Stock Market

Now, Ondo is one of the leading institutions bringing tokens to the equity market on Solana.

In January, the company added over 200 tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs to Solana. As of October, Ondo’s on-chain assets exceeded $500 million, whereas 1inch’s on-chain trade volume encompassed over 450 Ondo tokenized stocks and ETFs.

Securitize has more recently grown in their profile. In October, it began offering onchain U.S. stocks in Solana, with 12 stocks; it expanded to 25 stocks early in November. Standard investors can buy 1:1 backed security rights tied to firms like Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Tesla and Amazon.

More Traditional Securities Are Moving Onchain

With tokenized stocks, eligible investors have access to equity exposure on the blockchain and can transfer and settle their stocks through digital wallets. Not all tokens or tokenized stocks have the same rights attached to them; the term depends on the issuer.

With its increasing list of issuers and trading platforms, tokenized equities are coming off the fringe of niche experimentation into a general market onchain.

DTCC Plans Solana Integration for 2027

There may be still more institutional infrastructure on the horizon for next year. On Nov. 12, DTCC revealed it would integrate with Solana in the second half of this year to enable them to work together. The planned integration will enable eligible DTC-custodied securities to be tokenized on the network.

Those tokenized assets will have the same ownership rights, investor protections and regulatory safeguards that are provided for traditionally held securities, DTCC said. It currently handles tokenization of eligible equities, ETFs and the U.S. Treasuries and Solana is part of its larger multichain approach.
