title: Bitcoin Quantum Defense Could ‘Change the Value Proposition’ of BTC: Researcher
summary: Researchers behind SHRINCS have released a detailed security analysis of the proposed Bitcoin post-quantum signature scheme, bringing it closer to practical consideration while highlighting unresolved concerns about wallet safety, transaction costs, and implementation complexity. Bitcoin researchers...
content:
Researchers behind SHRINCS have released a detailed security analysis of the proposed Bitcoin post-quantum signature scheme, bringing it closer to practical consideration while highlighting unresolved concerns about wallet safety, transaction costs, and implementation complexity.

Key Takeaways

  • SHRINCS researchers released a security analysis of the proposed Bitcoin post-quantum signature scheme, establishing formal security arguments while acknowledging unresolved assumptions and the need for independent auditing.
  • SHRINCS combines smaller stateful signatures with a larger stateless fallback, seeking to minimize transaction fees and blockchain congestion. However, improper reuse of one-time signing keys could expose users to catastrophic theft risks.
  • Bitcoin’s growing quantum computing concerns are driving research into new cryptographic protections, but SHRINCS faces criticism over wallet security, implementation complexity, and transaction costs.

Bitcoin researchers have published a comprehensive security analysis of SHRINCS, an emerging post-quantum cryptography proposal designed to protect the network against future quantum computing attacks without sacrificing as much transaction capacity as competing solutions.

The 131-page analysis, dated Nov. 18, was authored by Blockstream researcher Mikhail Kudinov, with contributions from research director Jonas Nick and other collaborators. It provides a formal security argument for the proposed signature scheme, addressing a major outstanding requirement for the experimental technology.

The researchers evaluated SHRINCS against classical and quantum adversaries, reporting security bounds of approximately 121.4 to 122.7 bits against classical attacks under their analytical framework. The study also develops quantum security bounds, although some results depend on conjectures that remain unproven.

The document explicitly cautions that the proposal has not undergone an independent security audit and is not ready for deployment.

“We need all the possible feedback—engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov said, referring to the draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP), first announced in August. “There are a lot of things to check, test, complain about, or praise.”

Smaller Signatures Come With Security Trade-Offs

SHRINCS, short for Shrunken SPHINCS, uses SHA-256, the established cryptographic hash function already integral to Bitcoin, rather than introducing the different mathematical assumptions underpinning some alternative post-quantum schemes.

The design combines two signature methods under a single public key. Its primary, stateful mechanism produces signatures ranging from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while a stateless fallback generates signatures of 5,777 bytes.

Both are substantially larger than Bitcoin’s existing 64-byte Schnorr signatures, but the more efficient stateful option could help limit the blockchain congestion and higher transaction fees associated with a transition to quantum-resistant cryptography.

However, stateful signatures introduce a potentially catastrophic weakness if wallet software improperly reuses a one-time signing key for different transactions. Such a mistake could allow an attacker to forge signatures and steal funds.

“It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” Nick told MARA Foundation Head Isabel Foxen Duke during a video interview published Thursday. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.”

SHRINCS attempts to mitigate that danger by requiring wallets to permanently record each signing operation before producing a signature. If the signing state becomes unreliable, including when a wallet is restored from a seed phrase, then the software must switch to the larger stateless signatures.

The approach protects against unsafe key reuse, but could increase transaction costs for users recovering wallets or operating multiple devices.

“We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” Nick said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.”

The design has already attracted criticism. In an August review, researchers at Project Eleven argued that prioritizing blockchain efficiency could transfer unacceptable security risks to wallet users. They suggested considering a purely stateless alternative alongside changes to Bitcoin’s block capacity.

Ledger Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet has also raised concerns about wallet compatibility, hardware performance, and the difficulty of reproducing existing Bitcoin features, including certain multisignature arrangements and public-key derivation methods.

Bitcoin’s Quantum Countdown

The research arrives amid mounting attention to the potential threat that sufficiently powerful quantum computers pose to Bitcoin’s elliptic-curve cryptography.

As Bitcoin.com News reported in October, Google researchers demonstrated a quantum computing technique called magic state cultivation that reduced certain errors by a factor of 40, marking progress toward more reliable quantum computation.

Earlier Google research estimated that approximately 6.9 million BTC could potentially be exposed to future quantum attacks because their associated public keys have already been revealed. No existing quantum computer has demonstrated the ability to break Bitcoin’s cryptography, though researchers warn it could happen in a matter of years.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin developers are debating how to transition existing holdings to quantum-resistant addresses.

One particularly contentious proposal, BIP-361, would eventually prevent spending from vulnerable legacy addresses that fail to migrate within a proposed multiyear transition period. Critics warn that such an approach could permanently strand coins belonging to inactive holders.

SHRINCS addresses a different part of the problem: providing a practical cryptographic method for authorizing transactions once Bitcoin supports quantum-resistant signatures. Its adoption would still require additional protocol changes, extensive testing, and broader developer consensus.

The new security analysis represents progress toward that goal, but its authors acknowledge that several mathematical assumptions remain unresolved. Additional peer review, implementation testing, and consideration of real-world wallet behavior will be necessary before the scheme can be considered suitable for Bitcoin.

For now, the research underscores the central challenge facing Bitcoin’s post-quantum transition: protecting users against a future cryptographic threat without introducing dangerous new vulnerabilities or undermining the network’s ability to process transactions.

title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade could slip to May 2027 over compatibility concerns
summary: Ethereum developers are weighing changes to gas pricing proposals that could disrupt existing smart contracts, after contacting at least 50 affected companies.
content:
Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade could be pushed back as far as May 2027 if developers decide to modify its specifications to address smart contract compatibility issues, according to discussions at Thursday’s All Core Developers meeting.

Glamsterdam is a planned Ethereum hard fork aimed at increasing the network’s capacity and efficiency. However, blockchain security firm ChainSecurity warned in October that proposed changes to Ethereum’s gas pricing could disrupt existing smart contracts and potentially expose them to exploitation, prompting developers to postpone the Hoodi testnet fork, originally scheduled for Oct. 26.

The concerns center on gas repricing proposals EIP-8037 and EIP-8038. Researchers identified 13 real-world examples of potentially affected contracts in October, while a November investigation examined eight smart contract invariants that could be disrupted by the upgrade.

During Thursday’s meeting, developers said the Ethereum Foundation, ChainSecurity and security firm Dedaub had collectively contacted at least 50 affected companies. Three projects were classified as high impact, with fixes completed or expected by mid-December, while medium-impact projects reported timelines extending to Jan. 10.

Developers debated whether to retain Glamsterdam’s existing specifications or modify them to reduce compatibility risks, as changes intended to protect some contracts could disrupt others.

“Every spec change could, again, break new invariants that we are not aware of breaking yet,” one developer warned during the meeting.

Under the current specifications, mainnet activation could come as early as mid-January 2027. However, waiting until January to decide could push activation to late February or early March, or April or May if modifications are adopted, and no decision has been reached yet.

Related: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest

Ethereum weighs accelerating post-quantum security

Separately, Ethereum’s next planned hard fork, Hegotá, could see its scope reduced as the network seeks to accelerate its transition to post-quantum cryptography.

During the meeting, developers considered postponing some Ethereum Improvement Proposals to prioritize post-quantum features, although several argued that reducing the upgrade’s scope would offer little benefit unless it also shortened the rollout timeline.

Developers also raised compatibility concerns over EIP-8151, a proposal designed to protect accounts migrating to post-quantum security. A preliminary review identified a potentially large number of existing smart contracts that could be affected by the changes, complicating the proposal’s inclusion in Hegotá.

No decision was reached on Hegotá’s scope, with client teams expected to submit their positions ahead of further discussions in two weeks.

Key Takeaways:

  • USDT retains the lowest rating, 5, on S&P Global Ratings’ “Weak” side of the stability scale for stablecoins.
  • S&P reports that higher-risk reserve assets account for 28% of the USDT in circulation.
  • Tether stoutly contested the analysis, citing the nearly $8 billion in spare parts and cash.

Tether has responded to S&P Global Ratings, which had assigned its stablecoin USDT the lowest rating for its stability evaluation. S&P said the growing share of Bitcoin, gold and other higher-risk assets in Tether’s reserves remains a key concern despite USDT’s strong price-stability record.

  • S&P Keeps USDT at Its Lowest Stability Score
  • Tether Points to a Nearly $8 Billion Reserve Buffer
    • S&P Flags Regulation and Reserve Transparency
  • Tether’s Audit Adds Another Layer to the Dispute

S&P Keeps USDT at Its Lowest Stability Score

In November 2025, S&P rated USDT’s ability to sustain the dollar peg at 5, or below-average, as unchanged from the previous level.

The agency reported that assets it deems less secure, such as Bitcoin, gold, public equities, secured loans and corporate bonds, accounted for 28% of all its assets at the end of September, compared with 24% a year ago.

S&P reiterated its warning that a significant drop in those assets might compromise Tether’s cover cushion and make USDT undercollateralized.

Read More: Tether Bets $15M on Nomad to Push USDT and XAUT Deeper Into Brazil’s Crypto Market

Tether Points to a Nearly $8 Billion Reserve Buffer

The company’s own Sept. The results of the 30 financial figures for assets and liabilities indicated that there was $191.45 billion in assets and $183.50 billion in liabilities, which amounted to about $7.95 billion. These numbers were part of a report on Tether’s third quarter reserves, signed by BDO.

The short-term instruments, such as U.S. government securities and U.S. Treasury bills, are also extremely important to Tether’s reserve structure, as it reports $132.4 billion in direct and indirect U.S. Treasury bill exposure at the end of the quarter.

S&P Flags Regulation and Reserve Transparency

S&P also expressed concerns about the regulatory protections in which capacity Tether reserves are stored.

El Salvador’s stablecoin law has a minimum of 70% short-term liquidity requirement for assets held in reserve. Despite the rules, Bitcoin assets provided a lot of latitude, as do gold and loans; also, the rules do not include the same level of Mandatory segregation requirements as in some U.S. and European rules.

The agency also identified disclosure shortcomings, such as not having reserve custodians and counterparties identified publicly or providing reserve attestations every quarter instead of every month.

Tether’s Audit Adds Another Layer to the Dispute

Tether has acted to improve its financial reporting. In August, KPMG U.S. provided an unqualified opinion of Tether International’s 2025 financial statements. This is its first complete independent financial audit, Tether said, which kpmg reviewed assets, transactions, systems, valuations and counterparties.

S&P noted that the audited financial statements along with the full audit report were not available to them for the public review.

Notwithstanding the risks cited, S&P credited USDT with a good record of price stability, especially in the past year. The agency didn’t make further cuts because 5 already is the lowest score given in its scoring system.

The post JPMorgan Chase Discloses Vendor Cyberattack That May Expose...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • According to JPMorgan Chase, the attackers exploited JPMorgan-backed third-party companies.
  • The attackers may have obtained access to marketing records which include some customers’ names and email addresses.
  • Banking Services operate and customers will be provided with direct notification of services and free credit monitoring.

JPMorgan Chase has disclosed a cyberattack involving outside service providers, raising concerns about the security of customer information held beyond the bank’s own systems. The bank says it is continuing its investigation but has not reported any disruption to its services.

We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack.

Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.

There is no disruption to our services.

Where appropriate, we will contact affected customers directly and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring.

There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week.

— J.P. Morgan (@jpmorgan) November 19, 2026

  • Attack Involved Third-Party Service Providers
  • Marketing Data Exposure Raises Customer Privacy Concerns
    • JPMorgan Says Banking Services Are Not Affected
    • Affected Customers May Receive Direct Support

Attack Involved Third-Party Service Providers

JPMorgan Chase and its consumer banking brand Chase stated on X that enterprises on the banks’ network had been hacked. Its preliminary study shows that hackers gained access to some marketing information held by those vendors, the bank said. The details could contain users’ names and email addresses.

We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack.

Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.

There is no disruption to our services.

Where appropriate, we will contact affected customers directly and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring.

There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week.

— Chase (@Chase) November 19, 2026

The wording of the announcement implies that it was one involving data held by third-party service providers and not a confirmed breach of JPMorgan Chase’s core banking systems. The bank, however, hasn’t revealed the vendors or how the attackers were able to access the system.

Moreover, it hasn’t released a specific estimate regarding how many customers may have had their information exposed.

Read More: JPMorgan Cuts Polymarket Banking Ties Amid Regulatory Concerns and $20B Valuation

Marketing Data Exposure Raises Customer Privacy Concerns

The information the bank has found up to now is possible names and email addresses, which can still pose problems for customers involved.

Exposed contact information can be used by cybercriminals to send spoofed emails or to masquerade as a financial institution or to get other personal data. Consumers should be wary of unsolicited messages purporting to be from JPMorgan Chase or Chase that ask customers to sign in with private account numbers or other disclosures.

The bank did not confirm that there was access to financial account information, passwords or financial transactions records in the incident.

JPMorgan Says Banking Services Are Not Affected

The attack has not affected JPMorgan Chase’s operations. Its statement says that the customers can avail themselves of the bank’s services until the completion of the investigation. Some customers also had a different service disruption earlier this week, which was addressed during the announcement. The bank explicitly said the two incidents are unrelated.

It’s important because this may cause customers to conclude that the earlier disruption was the result of malicious activity. JPMorgan Chase have attributed the operational problem to something other than the cyberattack by the vendor.

Affected Customers May Receive Direct Support

If appropriate, JPMorgan Chase will reach out to Customers individually and provide services, such as complimentary credit monitoring. The bank has so far not provided more information regarding the investigation, the list of impacted vendors, the extent of the data exposure or the time of the attack.

The currently verified disclosures are as follows: third-party service providers targeted, possible access to marketing information, services unaffected.

title: Anthropic Stock (ANT) Debuts on Nasdaq at $1.5 Trillion Valuation in Record-Breaking IPO
summary: Anthropic is entering the public market with a record $81.3 billion IPO, pricing shares at $83 and setting a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ANT

Anthropic is entering the public market with a record $81.3 billion IPO, pricing shares at $83 and setting a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.

The Claude developer’s Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT marks a significant moment for the artificial intelligence industry, as investors assess whether its rapid revenue growth can support its extraordinary market valuation.

Anthropic Raises $81.3 Billion in Record IPO

Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on November 18, above its previously marketed range of $70 to $78. The offering includes 980 million Class A shares, making it the largest IPO by proceeds raised to date.

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives led by Dario Amodei, Anthropic reported $33 billion in nine-month revenue, marking year-over-year growth of more than 1,200%. Source: @WhaleInsider/X

Strong investor demand allowed the company to expand its original offering from 825 million shares, an increase of approximately 19%. Anthropic is selling 956,351,354 shares, while existing shareholders are offering another 23,648,646 shares. The company will not receive proceeds from the shares sold by those existing investors.

At the final offering price, the IPO generated approximately $81.3 billion in gross proceeds. The valuation reaches roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, accounting for securities such as stock options and restricted stock units. On a non-diluted basis, the company’s valuation stands at approximately $1.1 trillion.

The transaction also includes a separate $26 billion private placement at the IPO price, bringing the combined deal value to approximately $107.3 billion. This additional financing increases the capital available to support Anthropic’s expansion beyond the public offering itself.

Anthropic shares are scheduled to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker ANT. The listing process is expected to make the stock eligible for trading at approximately 10:00 a.m. ET, following the exchange’s opening procedures.

Claude Developer’s Revenue Surges More Than 1,200%

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives and researchers, Anthropic has developed into one of the most closely watched companies in the generative AI industry. Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei co-founded the business with a group of former OpenAI colleagues, positioning the company around advanced AI development and safety.

Anthropic’s $81.3 billion IPO surpassed SpaceX’s $75 billion offering in June 2026, setting a new record for the largest IPO in history. Source: @EconomyApp/X

Its Claude family of models has become the foundation of its commercial operations. The company’s offerings include consumer AI products, enterprise services, and developer-focused tools such as Claude Code, which has gained traction among software developers.

Anthropic’s latest financial disclosures highlight the speed of its expansion. Revenue reached $33.2 billion during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $2.5 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier. The increase represents year-over-year growth of approximately 1,206%.

Customer adoption has also expanded considerably. Anthropic reported more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annualized revenue over the preceding 12 months as of September 30. That figure compares with more than 950 customers a year earlier, illustrating the company’s growing presence among enterprise buyers.

The company also reported an annualized revenue run rate of approximately $81 billion as of October 31, according to its IPO disclosures cited by Reuters. This figure reflects the pace of business at that point rather than revenue already earned over a full year.

However, Anthropic has cautioned against assuming that its recent growth rate will continue. Its prospectus states, “We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates,” highlighting the uncertainty surrounding the long-term economics of the rapidly evolving AI market.

AI Infrastructure Spending Raises Profitability Questions

Despite its revenue expansion, Anthropic continues to face substantial expenses associated with developing, training, and operating advanced AI models.

The company’s SEC filing reported an operating loss of $1.3 billion for the first nine months of 2026, down from $5.2 billion in the same period of 2025. Although the reduction indicates an improvement in operating performance, the company has yet to establish consistent operating profitability.

Anthropic has committed approximately $900.9 billion to computing and infrastructure, with $70.7 billion due within 12 months of September 30, according to its final prospectus. Source: @IPONewsroom_/X

Computing requirements remain a central financial challenge. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure during the first half of 2026, according to Reuters. It incurred another $5 billion in computing costs during the third quarter.

The company has also committed to nearly $900 billion in future computing capacity through infrastructure partners, including Amazon and Alphabet’s Google. These arrangements are intended to provide the resources required to train and operate increasingly capable models.

Such commitments expose Anthropic to financing, infrastructure delivery, and demand-related risks. The company has warned in its regulatory filing that difficulties affecting its infrastructure partners could delay, reduce, or increase the cost of contracted computing capacity.

Competition presents another challenge. Anthropic faces pressure from OpenAI, Google, and developers of open-weight AI models, while some enterprise customers are also exploring the development of internal AI systems to manage costs.

The company’s ability to retain customers, improve computing efficiency, and maintain its position in enterprise AI will therefore remain important considerations for public-market investors.

Anthropic IPO Becomes a Test for AI Stock Demand

Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut arrives as investors reconsider the valuations and spending requirements of the broader AI industry. The company’s record fundraising demonstrates substantial demand for exposure to advanced AI development, even as concerns about infrastructure costs and future profitability remain.

The listing also provides an important reference point for other privately held AI businesses considering public offerings. Anthropic’s closest competitor, OpenAI, has also been discussed as a potential candidate for a future stock-market listing.

Investors will now have access to publicly traded Anthropic shares and regular financial disclosures, bringing greater scrutiny to the company’s revenue growth, operating expenses, capital commitments, and competitive position.

As portfolio manager Armina Rosenberg told Reuters, “One listing won’t settle the debate.” Her assessment reflects the broader uncertainty surrounding whether the economics of advanced AI can support the substantial valuations currently assigned to the industry’s fastest-growing companies.

For Anthropic, the $83 IPO price and approximately $1.5 trillion fully diluted valuation establish the starting point for its public-market journey. Its performance as a listed company will increasingly depend on converting rapid customer adoption into sustainable financial results.

Thursday, 19/11/2026 | 14:16 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Spreads on iSAM Securities' network run four times weekday levels, and 96% of weekend clients also trade Monday to Friday.
  • Its share of Saturday and Sunday turnover rose from 0.4% in June to 1.7% in October as more firms added it.

Most brokers offering gold over the weekend earn at least twice as much profit per million dollars traded as on weekday gold, iSAM Securities data show. Yet at every one of them, weekend trades are still under 0.1% of total gold volume, according to figures covering June to October.

The figures measure demand for a product brokers and liquidity providers have raced to launch. At least 19 firms announced a weekend or 24/7 gold product between February 17 and October 1, 14 of them in the third quarter, FM Intelligence counted.

The data come from Radar, a risk tool iSAM sells to retail brokers that pools information across the firms using it. The London-based liquidity provider added alerts in October for traders hedging across several brokers on the same network. It does not give a broker count.

London's trading industry is coming home!

A Fourfold Rise From a Small Base

Gold is taking a growing slice of weekend activity. Its average share of weekend volume at brokers offering it rose from 0.4% in June to 1.0% in September and 1.7% in October, iSAM said.

iSAM still advised caution. "It's unlikely that weekend gold trading should be a broker's priority," it wrote, citing current volumes.

The base explains why. At a typical CFD broker, weekend trading is about 0.2% of weekly volume, and almost all of it is crypto.

Other measures agree. Tapaas, another broker risk analytics firm, saw weekend gold trading roughly quadruple since June, LiquidityFinder reported, and CME Group's one-ounce gold futures drew about $60 million in their debut weekend in July.

The weekend traders are also not new clients. Of accounts trading gold at weekends, 96% trade it during the week too, which fits how CMC Markets pitched the weekend gold CFD it launched in April: a way to adjust positions before the Monday open.

Spreads Four Times Wider

The pricing favors the broker. Across the Radar network, the median weekend spread on gold is four times its weekday level, while Tapaas typically measured five to seven times at brokers with enough trades to compare.

Most brokers make at least double the profit per million dollars on weekend trades, measured ten minutes after execution , iSAM said.

That margin comes on top of holding costs clients already pay. All 32 broker accounts in a FinanceMagnates.com sample published in September charged negative overnight financing on gold longs.

For brokers, the risk comes at the Sunday reopen. Exchange liquidity in traditional products is thin over the weekend, so most brokers on the network hedge little, according to iSAM. Marked to market at the reopen, about half of them made money on weekend gold exposure and half lost.

Gold's weekend gaps this autumn were all under 0.5%, and iSAM noted that a large Monday gap has yet to occur.

Crypto exchanges price the metal differently. Binance's XAU/USDT perpetual held a one-tick spread 99.99% of the time over the past three months, iSAM said, but such venues often charge more than $500 per million in commission, against about $30 at the largest FX brokers.

Crypto exchanges price the metal differently. Binance's XAU/USDT perpetual held a one-tick spread 99.99% of the time over the past three months, iSAM said, but such venues often charge more than $500 per million in commission, against about $30 at the largest FX brokers.

Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands, November 19th, 2026, Chainwire

Anchorage Digital, Fluid, HoneyB, and Upshift support institutional and retail access to Bitcoin on Sui with BitGo, Inc. expected to follow in 2027

Hashi, Sui’s native Bitcoin finance infrastructure, is now live on mainnet, with more than 20 custody, retail, and DeFi participants.

Bitcoin has spent years becoming one of the world’s largest pools of capital. Now the infrastructure to put it to work has arrived, forming one of the broadest coalitions in Bitcoin finance. 

That coalition is still growing fast. The latest to join Hashi are Merkl, an onchain incentive platform; and Current, a lending protocol. These additions expand the ecosystem of DeFi products and services being built around Bitcoin on Sui.

Bitcoin-Native Finance, Now Live

Hashi keeps Bitcoin on the Bitcoin network and mints hBTC, a 1:1 Bitcoin-backed asset, on Sui. That hBTC can then serve as collateral for lending, borrowing, and other onchain financial products. 

Hashi is decentralized by design. It’s secured by validators, not a single entity, using industry-leading cryptography. On top of that foundation, it connects leading providers across custody, trading, and decentralized finance to build financial products, giving Bitcoin holders many ways to put their assets to work.

Accessing Bitcoin Finance on Sui

With hBTC now live, Bitcoin holders have a new set of opportunities at their fingertips. That starts with borrowing against BTC and accessing new financial strategies through lending markets and vaults. 

To meet the specific needs of institutions, several new providers are offering new lending and vault facilities. 

Fluid’s institutional-grade lending protocol is now live on Sui, beginning with Bitcoin-backed stablecoin loans. Bitcoin holders can use Hashi to bring BTC onto Sui as hBTC, then use it as collateral on Fluid to borrow stablecoins, starting with USDC with more flows coming.

summary:

content:
As financial markets become increasingly automated, the success of a liquidity desk depends on more than technology alone. It requires a combination of deep market expertise, fresh perspectives, and a culture that encourages knowledge sharing.

Ahead of Finance Magnates Summit London 2026 (FMS), we spoke with Finalto’s Group Head of Liquidity, Sam Horowitz, and members of his UK team about what defines a modern liquidity operation, why mentorship matters more than ever, and how the next generation of market professionals is shaping the future of institutional trading.

We want to reflect how Finalto is an agile, forward-thinking liquidity powerhouse that sustains its success through a dynamic blend of seasoned expertise and new perspectives.

The Evolution of the Modern Liquidity Desk

Talking to Sam Horowitz, we started by asking:

“You’ve navigated FX market shifts over a 30-year career and have spent the last year actively shaping Finalto’s liquidity and eTrading desk. From that vantage point, what is the biggest thing happening in liquidity provision right now that younger operators might be seeing for the first time?

[SH] Market crises come and go and are invariably powered by some unholy combination of greed, hubris and a profound failure of judgement. But for me the biggest change right now is in the use of AI as a force multiplier in our analytics processes. We’re doing so much more now with equivalent team sizes than even a couple of years ago. New industry entrants right now will increasingly see this as the norm, but for those of us with a slightly longer industry timeline, this definitely feels like revolution not evolution.

What is the most important quality you look for when building a modern liquidity team today compared to 10 years ago?

[SH] For me the most important quality of all hasn’t changed one iota in the 32 years I have been working in, and latterly building and running trading teams, and that’s integrity. In a marketplace where despite a massive increase in the use of data and modern tools, relationships and reputation still have a material effect on outcomes, how you conduct yourself matters.

[SH] Outside of that I think a curious mind and a genuine passion for market microstructure are essential, as is the technical skillset to interact with large datasets using modern tooling.

Which skills will be most valuable for liquidity professionals over the next five years?

[SH] Without question the ability to use modern (largely but not solely AI) tooling to answer increasingly complex business question using both empirical data and modelling. But also, crucially, to distil the answers back down into content able to be consumed by a wide range of ‘ley users’, and to be able to translate a theory and a model into a practical business focused solution. Frankly that’s a skillset that could be described as ‘evergreen’ as far as I am concerned.

Panel Teaser: could you give us a preview of the topics that you will address during the panel at FMS?

[SH] Well the panel title is “Be the Bank? Prime-of-Prime vs Direct Institutional Access” and essentially in a bit of a departure from the liquidity panel that normally we’d see at these events, we’re attempting in 40 minutes to unpick the question of what larger and more sophisticated retail brokers should be looking to do in terms of taking ownership of their liquidity. As a firm who value and continue to service the broker community, naturally we at Finalto have the view that we are a high quality and capital efficient way to access the wider market. Larger firms are increasingly looking to connect more directly with bulge bracket liquidity partners, and when they do so, have varying degrees of success and happiness in managing the infrastructure required to do this. There’s a lot of ground to cover here but I’ll attempt, along with my fellow panellists, to give some colour on what that looks like and how to go about considering the decision itself.

What misconceptions do younger professionals often have about liquidity when they first enter the industry?

[SH] That all the work is glamorous (when in reality we all spend time doing things that are intellectually more basic and less challenging than our academic training has prepared us for).

[SH] That only the larger institutions can offer a workplace and a job that requires intellectual rigour and where you can do meaningful work.

[SH] That physically being present and building a network is only a nice to have. To my mind even now it is an absolutely crucial part of navigating your career path. For my team I have encouraged them all to join the ACI’s Next Generation community in order to give them an intro to like-minded people in the industry and a seat at the table in shaping how our markets evolve.

For people mulling a career switch to eTrading and Liquidity Management, what would the skillset and profile need to look like to catch the eye of the hiring manager at a firm like Finalto?

[SH] Certainly all of the above. Interpersonal skills are hard to teach and to be honest sometimes hard to reliably hire for, but they’re a big part of the role still. In addition, ready-made skills in manipulating HFT datasets are core to our day-to-day here. Everyone codes, even me.

[SH] We run our analytics stack on a mixture of KDB, Python and SQL at Finalto, with dashboards in a mixture of Streamlit and Databricks, and all the recent hires had a coding and analytic test as part of the recruitment process.

[SH] It is a very different onboarding journey than would have been the case even 5-10 years ago (and certainly unrecognisable from my own route into the industry in the early 1990s). The setup at Finalto is much more akin to that you would see at a medium sized market making bank than a traditional broker, and the skillsets required to thrive here look increasingly similar.

The Next Generation in Action: How Under-30 Talent is Reshaping B2B Trading

Young professionals are the catalyst for innovation. Modern fintech firms bring together experienced market practitioners and technology-driven talent.

Today’s liquidity desks require a different skillset than they did a decade ago. Alongside market knowledge, firms increasingly seek expertise in data analysis, automation and technology-driven decision-making. As a result, a new generation of professionals is bringing fresh perspectives to institutional trading environments.

Where Experience and Innovation Meet

While technology continues to transform institutional trading, the most successful liquidity desks are those that combine innovation with experience. Understanding how younger market professionals approach data, automation and execution is becoming increasingly important for firms seeking a competitive edge.

As part of Finalto’s global liquidity team led by Sam Horowitz, we were in touch with Ulysse Sarron (UK / EU Liquidity Manager) and the team’s latest hires Daniel Paddock and Jeanne Gauthier

Ulysse Sarron, Finalto’s UK / EU Liquidity Manager

Having progressed within the industry, how do you see the role of liquidity management evolving over the next five years?

[US] I expect liquidity management to become increasingly proactive as desks develop a more sophisticated understanding of the data available to them. Across asset classes, understanding how client flow responds to market conditions gives us a stronger foundation for pricing and liquidity decisions.

Machine learning will play a greater role in identifying the relationships between flow, volatility and execution quality. Models could help forecast demand, detect changes in order book imbalance, and assess how consistently providers perform across different order sizes and market conditions. These insights should allow desks to make more informed decisions about their liquidity mix and pricing arrangements. The more demanding question is how well those models adapt when market behaviour changes.

I also see a practical role for agentic AI. An agent could quickly identify a deterioration in execution, investigate the underlying data and propose a course of action. Over time, I would expect some routine adjustments to take place within approved limits, with closer human oversight of decisions that materially affect pricing and execution.

This will place greater demands on liquidity managers. We will need to understand how these systems arrive at their conclusions, recognise their limitations and assess whether a proposed action makes commercial sense.

How do data and automation influence decision-making on today’s liquidity desks?

[US] They inform a substantial part of our work by allowing us to understand activity across the desk much more quickly and in greater detail.

Machine learning models can identify patterns in client activity. It can also detect changes in trading patterns that would be difficult to identify through manual analysis alone. That provides valuable context for managing flow and monitoring pricing from liquidity providers.

When assessing providers, quoted spreads are only part of the picture. We need to understand how competitive their pricing is at the sizes clients trade, how reliably those prices translate into successful execution, and how performance changes during periods of volatility. Examining spreads alongside fill rates, rejections, response times, slippage and other metrics gives us a more complete assessment. Machine learning can help identify the combinations of conditions under which a provider’s performance strengthens or deteriorates.

Automation brings that analysis into the daily workflow. Targeted alerts can identify deviations from expected performance, helping the desk prioritise investigations and hold more precise, evidence-based discussions with liquidity providers.

What qualities define high-performing liquidity professionals today?

[US] Proactivity is essential. Markets move quickly, and an approach that worked well yesterday may need revisiting today. That is particularly relevant when managing liquidity across asset classes with different trading patterns and sensitivities.

The strongest professionals combine curiosity with the discipline to follow an issue through. They notice changes, question unexpected results and take responsibility for understanding what is happening. Composure under pressure and clear communication are equally valuable, both within the business and in discussions with liquidity providers.

Effective monitoring supports all of this. Automated reports and alerts help us maintain oversight of a complex trading environment, while judgement determines which developments require attention and how urgently we should respond. For me, the ability to recognise a developing issue, take ownership and act early consistently contributes to better outcomes.

What’s the most valuable lesson you’ve learned from senior leaders?

[US] One lesson that has stayed with me is the importance of investing in relationships with liquidity providers. Those relationships are built through regular dialogue, honest feedback and an understanding of each other’s business. You need to be able to discuss the characteristics of the flow, explain what you are observing and consider the provider’s perspective.

That foundation becomes especially valuable when markets are volatile or execution quality changes. An established relationship allows for a more candid and productive conversation, making it easier to understand the issue and work towards a solution. Pricing matters, of course, alongside consistency, trust and the ability to work constructively together as conditions evolve.

You are speaking at the ACI Next Gen curated roundtable at FMSL, focusing on the views of the industry’s future leadership group. What do you expect to come out of that session?

[US] I expect AI and machine learning to feature prominently, particularly their practical application in our daily work. I am interested in hearing where people are finding measurable value, what has proved difficult to implement and how they are assessing the results.

I would also like the discussion to address how we develop the next generation of liquidity and trading professionals. As more tasks become automated, we need to consider how people acquire market experience, develop independent judgement and learn to manage relationships. Those capabilities deserve as much attention as technical proficiency.

For me, the value of the roundtable lies in bringing together people who face similar challenges from different perspectives. I hope we leave with practical ideas we can apply on our desks, a clearer understanding of the skills our industry will need, and relationships that allow the conversation to continue beyond the event.

Daniel Paddock and Jeanne Gauthier, Finalto’s Junior Liquidity and E-Trading Analysts

How did your technical data skills bring you to an institutional liquidity desk?

[DP] My route combined a computing BSc degree, a year working in financial crime data analysis, and an MSc in Computational Finance, where I brought programming and financial mathematics together through projects including a machine-learning options-pricing thesis. My interest in markets actually began with prediction markets: I was fascinated by how prices capture information and started building small projects to explore pricing inefficiencies. That curiosity eventually led me towards the MSc, and ultimately Finalto, where I now get to apply my technical skills to live market problems.

[JG] My studies in Mathematics and Finance at Imperial College London, along with my internships, gave me a strong foundation in statistics and data analysis. At Finalto, I apply these skills to understanding client flow, liquidity and execution quality.

How has working on a live liquidity desk challenged what you learned academically?

[DP] In education, problems generally come with a defined question, the necessary data, and a solution to work towards. On a real liquidity desk, deciding how to even frame the problem is a new significant part of the challenge. I have access to more real-world data than before – which for me feels like being a kid in a candy shop – but there are still questions that more data alone do not answer. This has taught me how much context, judgement and experience matter alongside the technical analysis.

[JG] On a live liquidity desk, context and client relationships matter, and you adapt your approach depending on the client.

Which emerging technologies will have the greatest impact on institutional trading?

[DP] For me, the obvious answer is AI, because of how much it is accelerating the move from an idea to a working prototype. In my own work, it gives me much more room to focus on the problem, the logic and the assumptions, and can help me turn an idea in the morning into something I can test later that day. I expect that shorter development cycles will make a significant difference to how quickly teams explore quantitative models and respond to new problems, with careful validation now carrying even more weight than before.

[JG] AI, particularly LLMs, could have a significant impact by using/ recalling relevant context to automate tasks.

How has working alongside experienced market practitioners shaped your own approach?

[DP] Working alongside experienced practitioners has taught me to take a step back before diving into the task: a piece of market context or a different interpretation can turn what looks to be complicated analysis into a much simpler approach. I now put much more emphasis on making my methodology – and especially my assumptions – clear and explainable. That allows me to bring my colleagues’ experience into the process earlier, helping me build better solutions.

[JG] Working with experienced colleagues has helped me better understand the context and how to adapt my approach to different clients.

content:
The Base-native leveraged prediction market platform expands its offering across crypto, global financial assets, sports and esports.

Toronto, November 19, 2026 – OmenX, a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform, today announced $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures alongside the launch of its on-demand, 30-second Bitcoin price prediction product.

The new product lets users predict whether Bitcoin’s price will rise or fall over the next 30 seconds, with each trade starting its own prediction window. A position opened at 10:00:12 runs until 10:00:42. Users can act when their view forms, with a full 30-second horizon, rather than adapting to the remaining time in a shared market round.

Featuring zero-slippage execution and rapid settlement, the product extends the familiar five- and fifteen-minute crypto prediction format to a shorter, individually timed experience. It adds to OmenX’s intraday offering, which spans prediction horizons from 30 seconds to 24 hours, depending on the market.

Beyond crypto, OmenX offers directional prediction markets linked to more than 100 global assets, including U.S. equities, futures, ETFs and indices. Its event markets also cover live sports and esports, with sports coverage spanning major football leagues, basketball, American football, ice hockey, baseball and UFC.

title: My Wallet Introduces 1:1 Cross-Chain Stablecoin Swaps After Being Listed First on WalletConnect
summary: Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 19th November 2026, Chainwire

Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 19th November 2026, Chainwire

Dubai, United Arab Emirates, November 19th, 2026, Chainwire

My Wallet users can now receive a different stablecoin on another blockchain at a fixed 1:1 token rate on eligible routes, with no spread, slippage or swap fee charged by the wallet

My Wallet, a self-custodial, open-source crypto wallet serving more than 10 million users, has launched 1:1 swaps for USDT, USDC, USDe and USDS across supported blockchains. On eligible routes, users can switch both stablecoins and networks within a single in-app flow, with the amount they will receive fixed before confirmation. 

The launch follows My Wallet’s listing at the top of WalletConnect’s WalletGuide. The wallet is also WalletConnect Certified and connects users to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

Simplifying Stablecoin Transfers Across Blockchains

According to research published in October 2026 by Coinbase and The Block Pro Research, organic stablecoin transfer volume exceeded $400 million per hour during Q3 2026. Yet stablecoins operate across multiple blockchains and token issuers, creating friction when users need a specific token on a specific network. Even when funds arrive on the right network, users may still hold the wrong stablecoin for a payment, trade or application.

My Wallet addresses this through its in-app swap aggregator, powered by LayerZero, NEAR Intents, and other bridges resulting in the best rate. On eligible stablecoin routes, the aggregator offers a fixed 1:1 token rate, with no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. My Wallet is the first among major crypto wallets to offer 1:1 swaps between different stablecoins across blockchains in a single in-app flow.

How the 1:1 Stablecoin Swaps Work

The fixed 1:1 rate can apply whether users switch to a different stablecoin or move the same token to another blockchain. On a supported cross-chain USDT-to-USDC route, for example, a user sending 10,000 USDT receives exactly 10,000 USDC. The same rate applies when the token stays the same: a supported transfer of 10,000 USDT from Ethereum to TRON delivers exactly 10,000 USDT on TRON.

The 1:1 option is available for swaps above $30 on supported routes. There is no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. Applicable blockchain network fees are paid separately, and the exact destination token amount is shown before confirmation. Other routes may have different rates and fees.

“Stablecoins are supposed to make moving money simpler, but users still have to think about which token they hold and which blockchain it’s on,” said Alexander Zinchuk, founder of My Wallet. “We’re removing that friction. If you hold USDT and need USDC on another network, you should be able to make that change in one step, know exactly how many tokens you’ll receive, and not pay an additional swap commission to your wallet.”

Native Bitcoin and Gasless EVM Transfers

The stablecoin launch follows the introduction of native Bitcoin support in My Wallet. Users can hold, send, receive and swap BTC alongside assets on Ethereum, Solana, TON and other networks, as well as buy Bitcoin with a bank card or sell it for fiat through MoonPay.

My Wallet now supports gasless transfers on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum and Optimism, adding to the existing support on Solana and TON. For these EVM transfers, the network fee is deducted from the tokens being sent, so users do not need to acquire a separate native token for gas. Supported assets are USDC on all five EVM networks, USDT on Ethereum and BNB Chain, bridged USDT on Base and Optimism, and USDT0 on Arbitrum. There is no minimum transfer amount or daily limit on the number of transactions.

Together, these innovative features advance My Wallet’s broader “All You Need to Enjoy Crypto” vision, combining asset management, seamless trading, and ease of use into one self-custodial app.

The new features are already available in My Wallet. Swap availability is subject to the selected assets, networks and routes.

About My Wallet

My Wallet is a self-custodial, open-source multichain wallet for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Hyperliquid, TON, TRON, BNB, Base, Robinhood, Monad, Arbitrum, Polygon, and more. Founded in 2022, My Wallet serves over 10 million users across mobile, desktop, web and its Telegram Mini App. The wallet has been audited by CertiK and ranks among the top-5 wallets on CertiK’s Wallet Leaderboard.

My Wallet is WalletConnect Certified and currently listed 1st in WalletConnect’s WalletGuide, connecting users to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

title: Crypto News Today: BTC Faces Miner Sell-Off, ETH Open Interest Rises, and XRP Faces Derivatives Pressure
summary: Bitcoin miner treasury sales, rebuilding Ethereum futures exposure, and renewed XRP derivatives activity are drawing attention as traders assess liquidity across digital assets.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH XRP

Bitcoin miner treasury sales, rebuilding Ethereum futures exposure, and renewed XRP derivatives activity are drawing attention as traders assess liquidity across digital assets.

Glassnode reports that public Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half of their tracked BTC reserves since January 2026. Meanwhile, Binance is driving renewed activity in Ethereum futures, while XRP traders are monitoring derivatives data for clues behind the token’s latest price decline.

Bitcoin Miners Sell Nearly Half Their Reserves Amid AI Expansion

Public Bitcoin miners are reducing their BTC holdings at an accelerating pace, marking a shift from the accumulation strategies that characterized much of the industry’s earlier development. According to a Glassnode chart published on November 18, combined Bitcoin reserves among tracked mining companies peaked in early 2026 before declining sharply as monthly net sales increased.

Glassnode data shows public Bitcoin miners have sharply reduced their BTC holdings since early 2026, accelerating sales recently to liquidate nearly half of their reserves. Source: @glassnode/X

Glassnode highlighted the change in miners’ treasury strategies, stating that “For years, listed miners held what they mined, and some bought more. Since January, they have sold nearly half their BTC.” The analytics firm linked the selling activity to growing investment in artificial intelligence data centers and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure.

MARA Holdings, Riot Platforms, and CleanSpark are among the publicly traded mining companies expanding their digital infrastructure businesses. Their strategies increasingly involve monetizing existing power capacity through data center development rather than relying exclusively on Bitcoin mining revenue.

Recent company disclosures illustrate the scale of this transition. MARA sold another 13,597 BTC after September, generating approximately $1.1 billion at an average price of $81,039 per coin. The company has now sold more than 40,000 BTC during 2026, according to its latest shareholder disclosures.

Riot Platforms also reported selling 20,264 BTC during the first nine months of the year, raising approximately $1.5 billion primarily to finance data center development. The company ended September with 2,418 BTC.

Its infrastructure expansion includes a 15-year agreement covering 910 megawatts of critical IT capacity at its Corsicana campus. The contract represents approximately $28 billion in potential revenue over its initial term.

CleanSpark is pursuing a similar strategy. The company secured a 20-year high-performance computing lease covering 175 megawatts of critical IT capacity, with approximately $6.6 billion in contracted revenue.

The shift does not necessarily represent an exit from Bitcoin mining. MARA has described its strategy as “not a pivot away from bitcoin,” emphasizing that mining remains the foundation of its operations while it develops additional revenue streams.

However, the scale of BTC disposals creates another potential source of market supply. With Bitcoin recently falling toward $62,000, continued miner selling could add pressure during an already weak trading environment. The available data does not establish miner sales as the sole cause of the decline, but the change in treasury behavior represents an important development for the market.

Binance Leads the Recovery in Ethereum Futures Open Interest

Ethereum’s derivatives market is showing signs of renewed positioning after an extended period of declining open interest and position reductions.

CryptoQuant data identifies Binance as the largest contributor to the recent increase in ETH futures open interest. The exchange’s activity has picked up as traders begin establishing new positions following the earlier unwinding of leveraged exposure.

The chart shows 24-hour open interest changes across exchanges, highlighting Binance’s significant contribution alongside ETH price fluctuations between $1,720 and $2,080 from November 11–18, 2026. Source: CryptoQuant via X

Data covering November 17–18 shows that open interest in Binance’s USDT-margined Ethereum perpetual contracts increased by approximately 2.82%, climbing from 2.2843 million ETH to 2.3486 million ETH. That represents an increase of roughly 64,400 ETH in outstanding contracts over the period.

The broader market chart also tracks ETH price movements between approximately $1,720 and $2,080 from November 11–18, reflecting considerable volatility during the repositioning process.

CryptoQuant contributor CW8900 has suggested that the reduction of existing positions is nearing completion, with traders beginning to establish new market exposure. The development could indicate a change in derivatives positioning after the earlier deleveraging phase.

However, rising open interest does not automatically indicate bullish sentiment. Every futures contract involves both a long and a short position, meaning increased activity can accompany either upward or downward expectations.

Ethereum’s price behavior also highlights this uncertainty. ETH closed at approximately $1,777 on November 18, down from $1,825 a day earlier, despite the increase in Binance open interest.

Consequently, traders will need to monitor additional indicators, including funding rates, liquidation activity, and spot market demand, to determine whether the renewed positioning reflects accumulating bullish exposure or an increase in bearish bets.

XRP Faces Derivatives Pressure as Traders Examine Spot Market Activity

XRP is experiencing another bout of selling pressure, with derivatives activity drawing attention as traders attempt to identify the source of the latest decline.

CryptoQuant-verified analyst CW8900 has attributed the downward pressure primarily to futures market activity, arguing that the spot market is not experiencing comparable net selling. The analyst stated that “There is no net selling in the spot market,” suggesting that leveraged trading could be amplifying short-term price movements.

CoinGlass shows XRP dropping from $1.007 to $0.970, with negative spot and futures CVD signaling strong selling pressure. Source: @CW8900/X

A CoinGlass chart provides additional context. The 15-minute XRPUSDT perpetual futures chart shows the token falling sharply from approximately $1.007 to $0.970. During the same observation window, cumulative volume delta (CVD) readings turned negative in both markets.

The chart recorded futures CVD at approximately -8.10 million and spot CVD at -8.16 million. These readings indicate that aggressive market selling exceeded market buying across the corresponding data sets during the selected period.

The negative spot CVD reading adds an important qualification to the analyst’s interpretation. Although CW8900 identifies derivatives activity as the primary source of downward pressure, the chart also shows aggressive selling within its selected spot-market sample.

CVD measures the difference between market buy orders and market sell orders over a given period. It can help distinguish between aggressive buying and selling activity, but it does not independently establish broader exchange inflows or total market-wide selling pressure.

A broader CoinGlass market snapshot on November 19 showed a different picture across a longer observation window. Futures recorded approximately $48.6 million in net taker selling over 24 hours, while spot markets registered around $1.8 million in net taker buying. This suggests that spot demand was absorbing some of the selling pressure from derivatives markets during that period.

The difference between the shorter CVD snapshot and broader trading-flow figures highlights why timeframe and market coverage matter when interpreting XRP trading activity.

For traders, the distinction is important. A derivatives-driven decline can produce sharp price fluctuations through leverage, liquidations, and changing futures positions without necessarily indicating sustained distribution across the entire spot market.

Nevertheless, the simultaneous negative CVD readings show that selling activity was not limited exclusively to perpetual futures during the chart’s selected interval.

What the Latest Crypto Market Data Shows

The latest developments highlight three different forces influencing Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP.

Bitcoin is facing additional potential supply as public miners liquidate treasury holdings to finance their expansion into AI and high-performance computing. Ethereum is seeing renewed futures positioning, with Binance accounting for a substantial share of the latest increase in open interest. XRP, meanwhile, remains sensitive to derivatives activity as traders examine whether futures selling is contributing to its price weakness.

Although these developments do not establish a common direction for the broader cryptocurrency market, they highlight changing capital allocation, leverage, and trading behavior across its largest digital assets. Further changes in miner reserves, futures positioning, and spot demand will help determine whether the current conditions represent temporary market adjustments or more persistent shifts in investor behavior.

title: XRP Price Today: $0.95 Support Holds, Gaussian Channel Flags $0.84 as a Potential Cycle-Bottom Zone
summary: XRP has recovered toward the $1 mark after recent weakness, but technical indicators continue to reflect a broader bearish trend.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

XRP has recovered toward the $1 mark after recent weakness, but technical indicators continue to reflect a broader bearish trend.

Traders are now monitoring the $0.95 support area and a longer-term Gaussian Channel level near $0.84 for potential signs of stabilization.

The latest XRP price rebound has coincided with improving momentum signals and reported whale withdrawals from exchanges exceeding $127 million. However, the recovery faces resistance from several moving averages, while a separate weekly chart analysis highlights the importance of maintaining a broader support structure to prevent further losses.

XRP Defends $0.95 Support But TradingView Signals Mixed Momentum

TradingView’s latest technical summary for XRPUSD on Bitstamp shows a price near $0.9991, up approximately 4.47% during the reported session. The recovery has brought the token back toward the psychologically important $1 threshold, although the broader technical rating remains Sell. The overall assessment includes 14 sell signals, seven neutral readings, and five buy signals.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The indicator breakdown highlights a difference between short-term momentum and the prevailing trend. Oscillators carry a Buy rating, with four buy signals, six neutral readings, and one sell signal. Moving averages, however, retain a Strong Sell assessment, reflecting 13 sell signals, one neutral reading, and only one buy signal. This divergence suggests that selling pressure may be easing, but a sustained trend reversal has not yet been established.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) on the 14-period setting stands at 26.23, placing it below the commonly watched 30 threshold for oversold conditions. The Commodity Channel Index (CCI) at -103.48 and Williams Percent Range at -85.85 also indicate that XRP has traded near the lower end of its recent range. These readings can precede short-term rebounds, although oversold conditions alone do not confirm a market bottom.

The MACD remains negative at -0.09623, providing a contrasting signal. Its bearish reading indicates that downward momentum has not fully dissipated. Consequently, the latest XRP price recovery needs further confirmation from price action, trading volume, and trend-following indicators.

XRP Accumulation Breakout and $127 Million Whale Withdrawals Support Recovery Narrative

Short-term momentum has shown signs of improvement following a two-day accumulation phase. CryptoQuant-verified analyst CW (@CW8900) reported that XRP broke above the upper boundary of its consolidation range, pointing to improving MACD and EMA readings.

XRP breaks above a two-day consolidation range, supported by bullish MACD and EMA signals. Source: @CW8900/X

In the analyst’s November 18 update, CW stated that XRP was showing an upward move after the accumulation phase ended. The accompanying chart highlighted a recovery following an extended decline from prices above $1.50. However, a breakout from a short consolidation range does not necessarily indicate that the broader downtrend has ended.

On-chain activity has also attracted attention. Reported net whale withdrawals from Binance exceeded $127 million between November 10 and November 18. Such movements can indicate that large holders are transferring XRP away from exchanges, potentially reducing immediately available selling supply. However, exchange outflows do not independently confirm fresh buying or long-term accumulation, as internal transfers and custody changes can also contribute to the figures. 

The broader market picture remains mixed. US spot XRP ETFs recorded approximately $19.1 million in net outflows during the November 9–13 period, according to figures reported by CoinCentral. This suggests that institutional investment flows have not yet provided consistent confirmation of the improving short-term momentum. 

Gaussian Channel Places $0.84 in Focus as Potential XRP Cycle-Bottom Zone

While short-term indicators point to improving momentum, longer-term technical analysis identifies another important level below the current market price. Analyst ChartNerdTA highlighted the upper regression band of XRP’s three-month Gaussian Channel near $0.84, describing it as an area worth monitoring during the current market correction.

XRP approaches the Gaussian Channel’s upper regression band near $0.84, a level historically associated with cycle bottoms and major market resets. Source: @ChartNerdTA/X

The analyst noted that this channel boundary has previously been tested around cycle bottoms and major market resets. Historical touches of the band are marked with red “RESET” circles on the long-term chart. The latest update suggests that XRP could approach the same technical region if the current correction continues.

ChartNerdTA also revisited an earlier warning from February 2026, when the analyst identified approximately $0.73 as a possible downside retest level. The current $0.84 channel reading provides a nearer reference point, although neither level guarantees a reversal. The analyst’s broader technical framework identifies the $1.80–$2.00 region as an invalidation area for the bearish setup.

The Gaussian Channel is a trend-following technical indicator that uses Gaussian filtering to establish price bands around a smoothed trend. Traders often use these boundaries to assess whether an asset is trading at an unusually extended level relative to its historical trend. However, its readings depend on the selected timeframe and settings, and historical support tests do not establish that the same outcome will repeat.

XRP Price Prediction: Key Support and Resistance Levels to Watch

Another weekly chart analysis by TradingView contributor VincePrince identifies a broader wedge formation that could influence XRP’s next major move. The analysis highlights an ascending trendline, the lower boundary of the formation and the 500-period exponential moving average (EMA) as important support references.

XRPUSD is forming a large descending triangle, with key support levels defined by the ascending trendline, lower wedge boundary, and 500 EMA. Source: VincePrince on TradingView

According to the analyst, XRP needs to maintain this support structure to establish the conditions for a potential reversal. A confirmed bounce could bring the chart’s upper target areas back into consideration. Conversely, a breakdown beneath the highlighted support would weaken the structure and expose the token to further losses.

TradingView’s moving-average readings also show why the recovery faces resistance. The 10-day EMA stands near $1.0205, while the corresponding simple moving average (SMA) is approximately $1.0163. Both remain above the reported market price and currently carry Sell signals.

The resistance structure becomes more pronounced across longer periods. The 20-day EMA sits near $1.0997, while the 50-day EMA is approximately $1.2161. The 200-day EMA stands around $1.3246. These levels represent potential resistance areas that XRP would need to reclaim to demonstrate a broader improvement in its technical structure.

On the downside, the $0.95–$0.98 region remains an important support band. TradingView’s Classic and Fibonacci pivot calculations both place the S2 level near $0.9775, while the Woodie S2 pivot sits around $0.9561. These overlapping references help explain why traders are monitoring this area closely.

A sustained move below $0.95 could shift attention toward the $0.84 Gaussian Channel level. However, the lower $0.62–$0.71 region identified by longer-term pivot calculations represents a separate downside reference rather than an immediate price target.

What Comes Next for XRP?

XRP’s immediate direction depends on whether buyers can defend the $0.95 support region and establish a sustained recovery above $1. The recent improvement in oscillators, the reported accumulation breakout, and exchange withdrawals provide several constructive signals. Nevertheless, the overall TradingView rating remains Sell, while the moving-average structure continues to reflect considerable overhead pressure.

A sustained move above the $1.02 area would provide an initial indication of improving short-term conditions. Further resistance between $1.10 and $1.13 could then become relevant. On the other hand, losing the $0.95 support region would increase attention on the $0.84 Gaussian Channel boundary.

For now, the $0.84 level remains a historical technical reference rather than a confirmed cycle bottom. Whether XRP can establish a durable recovery will depend on its ability to maintain support, overcome nearby resistance, and attract sustained buying interest.

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • HKMA and Swift are conducting cross-border payments trials with cross-border bank deposits in token format.
  • Project Ensemble will be investigating connectivity with the new digital ledger launching with Swift.
  • HSBC, Standard Chartered and Bank of China (Hong Kong) are all involved.

The development of tokenized bank money is also a big push for Hong Kong’s cross-border finance. To explore the capabilities of tokenized deposits to cross payment infrastructure and currency, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Swift are continuing their partnership.

  • Project Ensemble Moves Into Cross-Border Tokenized Payments
  • Tokenized Deposits Could Support Always-On Settlement
    • Swift Ledger Could Bridge Local and Global Digital Rails
    • Hong Kong Expands Its Tokenization Infrastructure

Project Ensemble Moves Into Cross-Border Tokenized Payments

The HKMA said the new work will examine interoperability between the settlement layer of Project Ensemble and the Swift ledger. The partnership involves Bank of China (Hong Kong), Standard Chartered Bank ( Hong Kong) and HSBC. The participants will consider mechanisms of payment based on deposits in multiple currencies in token form as a whole.

The objective is not to supplant the present banking frameworks with one blockchain framework. The project is experimenting, on the contrary, with the efficiency of borderless communication and transactions between separate regulated infrastructures.

But Swift already provides global connections for financial institutions and market infrastructures, handling transactions in 150 currencies. Its ledger effort will aim to help link emerging digital-value platforms while keeping banks in the regulated financial wheel.

Read More: DBS and Citi Enable 24/7 USD Payments With Tokenized Deposits, Cutting Settlement to Minutes

Tokenized Deposits Could Support Always-On Settlement

The tokenized deposits are a digital-token version of commercial bank funds. They are bank liabilities instead of non-bank private issuers’ stablecoins.

The collaboration is examining the possibilities of tokenized deposits and interoperable infrastructure to facilitate real-time, always on and programmable cross border transactions, said Howard Lee, the deputy chief executive of the HKMA.

That aligns perfectly with Hong Kong’s recent enhancement of EnsembleTX to facilitate 24/7 settlement of interbank tokenised deposit transfers via tokenised central bank money.

The enhanced capability was launched by HKMA on 2 Nov for participating institutions to settle transactions outside the traditional banking hour. Currently, 12 banks and 20 pioneers in the industry are involved in the pilot.

Swift Ledger Could Bridge Local and Global Digital Rails

Project Ensemble International, the Swift connection, brings the international flavor to Project Ensemble. Since 2023, HKMA has been collaborating with Swift on interoperability among digital currencies. The most recent move takes the focus from standalone domestic experiments to commercial bank tokenized deposits and cross border use cases.

Banks might benefit because with interoperability they would have to invest less in establishing technical connections independently with all the digital-asset networks they use.

The company will look at ways its ledger can link to new domestic digital platforms from multiple countries and facilitate faster settlements, said Swift Chief Business Officer Thierry Chilosi.

Hong Kong Expands Its Tokenization Infrastructure

Project Ensemble is moving beyond early testing toward broader commercial applications.

The next phase will be to develop more activities around tokenized deposits, tokenized money and tokenized investment products, HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission said. Additionally, Hong Kong has permitted 24/7 secondary trading for some tokenized money market funds.
