title: Etherscan Investigates Unauthorized Access Attempts Targeting Its Freshworks System
summary:
Key Takeaways: Etherscan detected unauthorized access attempts to its Freshworks customer-support and ticketing system on November 18, 2026. The investigation is ongoing with precautions, but no data exposure or successful
The post Etherscan Investigates Unauthorized Access Attempts Targeting Its Fr...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Etherscan detected unauthorized access attempts to its Freshworks customer-support and ticketing system on November 18, 2026.
  • The investigation is ongoing with precautions, but no data exposure or successful breach were confirmed.
  • Users are warned to avoid suspicious support messages and never provide private keys, seed phrases or passwords.

Etherscan has issued a security alert after detecting an attack on customer support infrastructure. The whole incident has drawn warnings of potential impersonation attempts against cryptocurrency users.

Security Notice: Reminder Regarding Etherscan Support Communications

Earlier today, we detected attempts to gain unauthorized access to our customer support and ticketing system (Freshworks).

We are currently investigating the situation and taking precautionary measures.

In the meantime, we would like to remind all users to exercise caution when communicating with anyone claiming to represent Etherscan Support.
– Never share your private keys, seed phrases, passwords, or other sensitive information.
– Be cautious of unexpected links, attachments, or requests for sensitive information, even if they appear to come from our official support channels.

As a general reminder, Etherscan Support will never ask for your private keys or recovery phrases.

We are taking this matter seriously and will provide further updates if necessary.

Thank you for your understanding and continued trust.

— etherscan.eth (@etherscan) November 18, 2026

  • The Attempt Targeted Etherscan’s Support System
  • Etherscan Warns Users against Fake Support Communications
  • Crypto Users Should Be Careful with Support Requests

The Attempt Targeted Etherscan’s Support System

On November 18, Etherscan announced that it had detected hackers trying to log into its customer-support and ticketing system, which is provided by third-party Freshworks. The company’s team was investigating the activity and taking precautions, said in a notice posted on X.

Read More: Etherscan Launches RobinScan for Robinhood Chain, Opening Access to 4,663 Chain Data

Etherscan, however, has yet to release more details on the attempts technically. There are no details on how this activity had taken place, who was involved, or whether such attempts had succeeded in accessing it. It has also not said if they had gained access to support tickets, emails sent to customers or user contact information.

Its publicly listed services might had remained available during the incident, as Etherscan’s status page continued to list its mainnet website and API as operational.

Etherscan Warns Users against Fake Support Communications

In addition to investigating, Etherscan issued a warning to users to be vigilant when receiving unsolicited messages, links, attachments, or requests for confidential information.

The company especially cautioned that fake communications may come from official support channels. It also emphasized an essential security policy: Etherscan Support will never ask for private keys or recovery phrases.

This warning is particularly important for cryptocurrency holders, as wallet keys grant access to digital currencies. A user’s seed phrase/private key, if obtained by attackers, can allow an attacker to control the wallet and move the funds.

Crypto Users Should Be Careful with Support Requests

Etherscan is a blockchain explorer that lets users search through the Ethereum transactions, view wallet addresses and get on-chain information. It does not function as a custodial wallet, hold users private keys or manage users transactions. This means that its support team has no power over blockchain transactions or getting back the lost cryptocurrency.

This separation makes wallet credentials requests very suspicious. Users are advised not to provide passwords or recovery phrases or private keys to any user or entity pretending to be Etherscan. The incident also demonstrates the danger of third party customer support websites. These systems may include information such as user messages and contacts that attackers could potentially use in targeted phishing attacks.

Previously similar incidents have occurred. For instance, hardware wallet provider Trezor had its third-party support ticketing system compromised in January 2024, potentially exposing the names and email addresses of as many as 66,000 individuals.

The metal gained a bit of ground in November to above $4,100 but has sold off a lot of those gains since then. It continues to be on a downward path, cutting prices back down to the $3,875 area.

But there are signs of less selling pressure, as momentum readings improve. Meanwhile, there is a split between further weakness in the near term and recovery into the longer term by 2027. Three technical angles show areas and conditions traders need to watch before the weekend.

Gold Price Struggles Below $4,000

The metal opened at $3,870.91 and has risen 0.13% over the past candle. The big picture, however, is bearish since gold has pulled back from its August highs of around $4,680. The downward trend continued in September and October, with sellers setting lower highs.

content:
Skip to content
Assets: DOGE

Dogecoin (DOGE) is testing a critical $0.052–$0.06 support zone as surging Bitfinex long positions and oversold conditions raise hopes of a potential bullish reversal.

According to Brave New Coin, Dogecoin recently traded near $0.06376 following a sharp decline, bringing the price closer to a major historical support zone between $0.052 and $0.06 that previously held during the 2022–2023 bear market.

Despite increasing long positions on Bitfinex, DOGE price remains under pressure across higher timeframes, with the weekly Ichimoku Cloud continuing to reflect bearish momentum.

Dogecoin Returns to Major 2022-2023 Support

Dogecoin has now fallen back into the same broad price region that repeatedly attracted buyers during the 2022-2023 bear market. Daan Crypto Trades highlights a higher-timeframe support band around roughly $0.052-$0.06, with DOGE currently sitting near the upper end of that zone.

That makes the current reaction more important than an ordinary short-term dip. DOGE price spent a considerable amount of time building around these levels before the previous cycle recovery developed, and another strong defense would suggest that long-term buyers are beginning to become active again.

The structure is still weak, however, DOGE remains far below the major highs formed during 2024 and 2025, so holding support is only the first step. A sustained breakdown through the lower end of the zone would remove one of the strongest technical floors still visible on the chart and leave the market searching for a new base.

Dogecoin has returned to the higher time-frame support. Source: Daan Crypto Trades via X.

Ichimoku Shows DOGE at a Critical Turning Point

The weekly Ichimoku structure reinforces how significant the current area has become. DOGE is trading near $0.059-$0.06 while remaining well below the Ichimoku cloud, which continues to slope lower and reflects the broader bearish trend that has dominated much of 2026.

Price has also remained beneath the key Ichimoku lines, showing that momentum has not yet shifted back toward buyers. At the same time, DOGE price is now pressing into a horizontal support region where previous declines have started to slow.

Dogecoin is testing long-term support while the weekly Ichimoku structure remains bearish, making the reaction around $0.06 increasingly important. Source: CryptoSays via X.

That leaves the chart at an important decision point. A strong reaction from current levels could begin the process of rebuilding momentum, but the first meaningful improvement would still require DOGE to recover the short-term Ichimoku levels above price. Until then, the cloud remains an overhead barrier, and the larger trend remains under pressure.

DOGE Technical Analysis

Dogecoin is now trading at a technically important area after sliding back toward the $0.058-$0.059 region. The daily chart shows a sharp selloff into support, with price briefly dipping under recent lows before stabilizing just above the broader $0.0518 support zone. At the same time, RSI has dropped into oversold territory near 27, which usually tells you selling pressure is getting stretched even if the trend itself is still weak.

Dogecoin is trading at around $0.0637, down 4.77% in the last 24 hours at press time. Source: Brave New Coin

That does not mean DOGE price has already bottomed, but it does mean the market is reaching a zone where reactions become more likely. If buyers can hold the current area and build a bounce, the first recovery levels come in around $0.064 and then $0.067-$0.070, where the recent breakdown started to accelerate. If DOGE loses the current base more decisively, then the $0.0518 region becomes the key support to watch, because a clean break below that would weaken the structure further and leave the market searching for a deeper floor.

Bitfinex DOGE Longs Surge Near the Market Lows

Positioning beneath the market is starting to tell a more bullish story. Data shared by The Money Ape shows Bitfinex DOGE long positions rising sharply, with exposure jumping from around the mid-5 million range to more than 7.1 million in a very short period.

The timing makes that buildup particularly interesting. These positions are being opened while DOGE trades close to its higher-timeframe support rather than after a large recovery, suggesting that larger traders are beginning to position aggressively around the current weakness.

That does not mean price has already bottomed, but the size of the increase shows that conviction is building on the long side. If DOGE begins holding the current support region and price starts recovering, the derivatives positioning could become one of the stronger early signs that traders were accumulating ahead of the move.

Bitfinex DOGE long positions have climbed above 7.1 million. Source: The Money Ape via X.

Dogecoin Fundamentals Strengthen With DogeOS Expansion

Dogecoin’s fundamental story is starting to broaden beyond payments and speculation. DogeOS is working to bring EVM-compatible smart contracts into the ecosystem, with DOGE expected to act as the gas token, giving the asset a more direct role in application and on-chain activity.

If adoption follows, that could add a new source of demand for DOGE and strengthen its utility case over time. For a project still widely viewed through its meme identity, expanding into smart contracts and application activity would mark an important step toward a more developed ecosystem.

DOGE Bulls vs Bears: What Changes the Trend?

The bullish side now has two arguments working in its favor: Dogecoin is sitting on a major historical support region, while Bitfinex traders are aggressively increasing long exposure around the same area. If buyers can continue defending the low-$0.06 region, the market would have a stronger foundation for a broader recovery.

The bearish argument is still visible in the trend itself. DOGE price remains below the weekly Ichimoku structure and has yet to produce the kind of higher high that would confirm sellers are losing control. A bounce therefore needs to develop into an actual trend change rather than another temporary reaction from support.

For bulls, reclaiming roughly $0.07-$0.08 would be the first meaningful improvement. A move back through $0.09-$0.10 would carry considerably more weight and begin turning the current base into a larger recovery structure.

title: US Senators Question SEC Tokenized-Stock Exemption Over Wallet Transfers and Investor Protection
summary: Four Democratic US senators have pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission for answers about how its new approach to tokenized stock trading will protect investors.
content:
TL;DR

  • Four Democratic senators challenged the SEC’s tokenized-stock trading exemption in a new letter.
  • Their concerns include wallet-to-wallet transfers, AML checks, pricing and issuer protections.
  • The letter seeks clarification and oversight; it does not itself revoke the exemption.

Four Democratic US senators have pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission for answers about how its new approach to tokenized stock trading will protect investors and prevent illicit transfers. Their November 16 letter, reported by The Block, takes aim at gaps they see in the SEC’s five-year innovation exemption for certain trading venues. The development is an oversight challenge, not a court ruling or a notice that the exemption has been cancelled. It goes to a central difficulty for tokenized securities: a regulated purchase can become a blockchain transfer to another address.

What the exemption is intended to enable

The SEC introduced its approach in September, allowing qualifying tokenized-securities venues to operate under a defined exemption from some ordinary exchange-registration requirements. The aim is to permit experimentation with trading stocks in token form while the agency assesses a new market structure. A token representing a security still raises questions about ownership, trading rules and investor rights. The exemptions and their precise conditions matter more than a general statement that securities have moved on-chain. Not every blockchain token, broker or venue automatically qualifies for the same regulatory treatment.

The lawmakers’ main concern

Senators Angela Alsobrooks, Ruben Gallego, Mark Warner and Catherine Cortez Masto reportedly told SEC Chair Paul Atkins that the framework lacks sufficiently specific safeguards around know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering procedures. A buyer verified by a regulated venue might later transfer a token to a wallet whose controller has not undergone the same checks. This problem is not solved merely by verifying the identity of the first purchaser. The letter asks how secondary transfers and the reach of compliance obligations would be managed once tokens circulate beyond the initial venue.

For related context, see our earlier report on Hong Kong's developing licensing rules.

Investor pricing and issuer rights also feature

The senators raised concerns about retail-investor protections and pricing, and reportedly asked whether companies could opt out of having their shares tokenized. Those questions are distinct from financial-crime screening. A token that references equity needs a clear relationship to the rights and obligations of the underlying security, as well as fair information about execution and ownership. If an issuer’s wishes, the investor’s expectations and the platform’s legal structure do not line up, technical transferability alone cannot resolve the conflict. Policymakers must address those issues in enforceable terms.

What happens next

The lawmakers asked the SEC to explain its approach and urged a transparent rulemaking process for changes in the regulatory treatment of tokenized securities. Such a letter can affect oversight and public debate, especially as control of congressional committees changes, but it is not itself binding legislation. Venues exploring tokenized equities should continue to follow the actual exemption terms and any subsequent SEC guidance. The next concrete milestones are the agency’s response, proposed revisions if any, and how early trading models implement identity, custody and transfer restrictions.

A workable compromise, if one emerges, may turn on which transfers are allowed after a regulated initial sale. Some token designs can restrict transfers to approved addresses, while others rely on venue-level checks or additional intermediaries. Each model gives up something different in portability, privacy or market openness. The senators' concerns therefore reach beyond rhetorical support for or opposition to blockchains: they ask what compliance guarantees exist when a security is represented by a programmable token that can move outside its original trading environment.

For related context, see our earlier report on new institutional crypto-custody arrangements.

Tokenization can change how securities move, but it does not automatically settle which rules should accompany them. The dispute now concerns the design of that regulatory perimeter, with no basis to describe the senators’ letter as an immediate prohibition on tokenized stocks.

Reporting sources: The Block report of four senators’ letter

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

TL;DR

  • Investigators tracked 34,279.66 ETH from a Binance hack-linked address to three new wallets.
  • The movement was worth roughly $63 million at the reported market price.
  • No verified exchange deposit or executed sale had been established in the initial reports.

A wallet linked by blockchain investigators to the October 29 Binance breach has transferred 34,279.66 ETH to three newly created addresses, ending a period of inactivity. The ether was worth roughly $63 million at prices used in Tuesday’s reporting. That is a significant movement of suspected stolen funds, but a wallet transfer is not automatically a sale, a successful laundering step or proof that the recipient controls are independent of the sender. Investigators had not identified the new addresses as exchanges at the time of their initial reports.

The new transactions are visible on-chain

Monitoring groups MistTrack and Solid Intel reported the transfers on November 17. MistTrack described three movements of approximately 12,000 ETH, 12,000 ETH and 10,279.66 ETH. The receiving wallets were newly created, and the monitored funds had not moved again when the analysts published their findings. Public transaction records make it possible to trace the amounts and destinations, but they do not disclose the human operator behind each address. The link to the earlier breach rests on investigators’ attribution of the sending wallet, not a label embedded in the blockchain itself.

The wider breach remains unresolved

The October attack involved vastly larger losses than Tuesday’s movement. US investigators attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking group, and authorities have announced substantial asset restraints and seizures. Blockchain intelligence firms have also tracked funds moved through different assets and protocols. These parallel developments should not be added together casually, because frozen, seized, recovered and still-controlled amounts describe different legal and operational states. The fresh ETH transfers are one piece of a complex post-incident trail rather than an update to the full net-loss number.

For related context, see our earlier report on Coinbase's custody and security precautions.

Movement does not establish selling pressure

Crypto trading commentary sometimes treats any transfer from an exploit-linked wallet as preparation to dump tokens. That can happen, but the evidence here does not yet establish a market sale. Transfers may consolidate funds, redistribute control or precede another operation. Until an address is linked to a trading venue, bridge, mixer or other service, the immediate observable fact is the destination change. Even a later exchange deposit would need careful interpretation: deposits are not identical to executed sell orders. Reporting should preserve those steps rather than collapsing them into one dramatic conclusion.

Why transparency helps, and where it stops

Ethereum’s public ledger lets investigators monitor known addresses and alert service providers if assets reappear at identifiable points. Token issuers, exchanges and law enforcement may each have different powers depending on the assets and jurisdictions involved. Native ETH cannot simply be frozen by an issuer in the way some centrally administered tokens can. That difference complicates recovery when funds leave services that can intervene. The next useful evidence will be further movements, identification of services receiving the funds and official updates to the case.

Investigators can improve attribution confidence by comparing the sequence, amounts and transaction timing with addresses already associated with the incident. Yet public labels can be incomplete, and a newly created wallet may simply be another address controlled by the same actor. Readers should resist claims that funds have reached a criminal group, a particular country or a cash-out desk unless that identification is supported by additional evidence. Future investigative notices should specify their degree of confidence and distinguish observed transfers from hypotheses about their purpose.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Unocoin wallet compromise.

The latest transfer warrants close monitoring, but it should not be reported as the disposal of $63 million in stolen ether without further proof. The distinction between observable transactions and inferred intent is especially important in a security incident of this scale.

Reporting sources: CoinDesk report of MistTrack and Solid Intel monitoring · MistTrack transfer report
